Police have confirmed that a body discovered in a Devon river is that of missing teenager Taylor Charlton.

The teenager, aged 15, was last seen on the night of 8 May, prompting an extensive search operation.

His remains were found in the River Taw on 24 June, with police now formally identifying him.

A Devon and Cornwall Police spokesperson said: “This is not the outcome that anyone hoped for and we know how deeply this will affect the local community who have shown tremendous support throughout the search.

“An investigation into the circumstances surrounding Taylor’s death remains ongoing and detectives will continue to establish the full facts.”

Taylor, from Barnstaple, was 14 at the time he went missing but has since had a birthday.

open image in gallery Taylor Charlton’s remains were found in the River Taw on 24 June, with police now formally identifying him ( Devon and Cornwall Police )

Police were called to the River Taw near Sticklepath, Barnstaple, at 4.20pm on June 24 after human remains were seen in the water.

Two people arrested in the investigation into his disappearance remain on police bail while inquiries continue.

The force urged the public to help the investigation by avoiding speculation and not sharing unconfirmed information online.

It also asked for the privacy of the boy’s family to be respected.

“Taylor’s family have been updated of this development and our thoughts and condolences are with them, Taylor’s friends and the local community,” the spokesperson added.

Anyone with information that may assist our enquiries is asked to contact police by calling 101 quoting reference number 50260117084.

A new federal initiative seeks to ensure Mexican train crews transporting freight across the U.S. border can comprehend vital safety information in English, while also protecting American jobs from the use of foreign labor.

The proposed rule, announced Friday by the Trump administration, aims to strengthen certification standards for safe train operations. Two major rail unions have praised the measure.

However, Union Pacific and CPKC, the two railroads most directly affected by potential restrictions on Mexican crews, did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The Association of American Railroads, a trade group, declined to comment, stating it is studying the new regulation.

This action follows December letters from the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) to CPKC and UP. These communications were prompted by inspections that found train crews often had difficulty understanding English. The government urged the railroads to reexamine their practices, ensuring Mexican crews are English-proficient and do not operate trains more than 10 miles (16 kilometers) inside America.

Two major rail unions praised the proposed rule ( Brandon Bell/Getty Images )

Last fall, federal inspectors found numerous problems in Union Pacific’s Eagle Pass rail yard and CPKC’s facility in Laredo where train crews were having a hard time understanding operating bulletins and U.S. regulations that require information about hazardous materials and emergency responses to be maintained in English.

At that time, both UP and CPKC pledged to make sure they were following the existing rules, but now the federal government wants to strengthen them “because railroad crews must be able to communicate fully and accurately when crossing into the United States, most notably with dispatchers and emergency responders during a crisis, as a safety-critical function.”

This rail safety effort aligns closely with the Transportation Department's efforts to ensure that truck drivers can understand English, so they can read road signs and warnings and communicate with first responders after an accident or during an inspection. The government has tried to withhold millions of dollars in highway funding from New York and California because it isn’t satisfied with the steps those states have taken to make sure the commercial driver’s licenses they issue are valid.

Mark Wallace, the national president of the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen union, has been raising concerns about this practice of using Mexican train crews for several years because of safety, security and job concerns.

The union has said that the handoffs used to happen right at the border, but now Union Pacific and CPKC routinely ask Mexican crews to bring trains several miles over the border to one of their railyards where the crew switches can be done more safely. But the firm 10-mile (16-kilometer) restriction in this rule will prevent the railroads from expanding this practice to railyards further into America like the union said UP was considering in New Mexico.

Wallace said the language barrier would pose a hazard in the event of issues such as a derailment.

The SMART-TD union that represents conductors and other rail workers also said the provisions of the rule that will prohibit train crews from using a system that's similar to cruise control for freight trains when they take their certification tests will help ensure they can operate a train safely.

“Railroad certifications should represent proven ability, not simply possession of a certificate,” said Jared Cassity, who is SMART-TD’s top safety expert. “When lives are on the line, the FRA must know that an engineer can safely operate a train, not just supervise a computer doing it.”

Massachusetts is on the way to giving doctors the final say on whether an abortion should be allowed late in pregnancy, a move expected to affect few cases but that supporters say is needed because hospitals are now turning away women they should be serving.

The state Senate adopted the measure Friday, sending it to Democratic Gov. Maura Healey, who has signed other laws strengthening abortion rights.

Under current Massachusetts law, abortion is legal for the first 24 weeks of pregnancy. It is allowed after that only if a physician using best medical judgment says it is necessary to preserve the life, physical or mental health of the woman, because of a lethal fetal anomaly or diagnosis or because the fetus wouldn't likely survive outside the uterus.

State Rep. Christine Barber said that under that framework, hospitals turned away some women for abortions late in pregnancy, even in a case where a fetus had a stroke and was determined to be unlikely to survive.

The new law would take out the list of specific reasons and say simply that it would be allowed “based on the professional judgment of the physician.”

Opponents say that it would allow abortion until birth — even on healthy fetuses — and that later abortions are more complex and risky for the women.

“While this legislation prioritizes access, it does not prioritize a woman’s safety,” Myrna Maloney Flynn, president of Massachusetts Citizens for Life, said in a video encouraging supporters to tell lawmakers to reject the bill.

Abortion law changes have slowed but not stopped

If Healey signs it, the law would be the latest change to a U.S. abortion landscape that received a shock four years ago after a Supreme Court ruling that overturned Roe v. Wade and allowed states to enforce abortion bans.

Some already had bans on the books as they waited for permission to enforce them, and others adopted bans or restrictions after the ruling. Currently, 13 states are enforcing bans abortion at all stages of pregnancy, with some exceptions. Another four bar it after about six weeks of pregnancy — which is often before women realize they are pregnant.

Several Democratic-controlled states have moved the other way, adding laws that seek to protect medical providers from prosecution for providing abortion to patients in other states. Massachusetts is among the states that has gone farthest, with a shield law that applies to those who prescribe abortion bills via telehealth to women in states where abortion is banned. Anti-abortion officials in Louisiana and Texas are testing those protections.

Most abortion-related state laws adopted this year have not made for major changes on when or how abortion is allowed.

For instance, a new Colorado law requires colleges that have student health centers to provide abortion pills for students starting in August 2027. Private schools that say it conflicts would their religious beliefs would be exempt.

A new Oklahoma law makes it a felony to buy or sell those pills for the purpose of an unlawful abortion for someone else.

Europe faces a fresh border crisis after around 60,000 migrants from Morocco crossed into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta in just 24 hours.

At least 57 people died as border security struggled to deal with the sudden influx, with extraordinary footage capturing the huge crowds making their way into Spain’s North African territory.

Some drowned in the crossing while others were killed in a stampede at the Tarajal beach fence near a border checkpoint with Morocco.

Spain’s prime minister Pedro Sanchez called the incident an “attack on Spain’s territorial integrity” and vowed to “use all the resources of the state to guarantee security and coexistence”.

open image in gallery Migrants attempting to cross into Ceuta gather on a hilltop during clashes with Moroccan security forces ( AFP/Getty )

Ceuta and the larger Spanish territory of Melilla, which is some 400km (250 miles) east of it, are located on the Mediterranean coast at the tip of Africa. They hold the European Union’s only land borders with Africa.

Andy Burnham, called the scenes a “cause for concern” as the shadow home secretary Chris Philp warned Spain’s border crisis could “rapidly become our border crisis”.

The incident has also sparked a diplomatic row across Europe with Italy’s prime minister Giorgia Meloni calling for Spain’s suspension from the Schengen Agreement.

Thousands of people were seen attempting to breach the border by land and sea by swimming around coastal barriers and forcing their way through land-border infrastructure. It is one of the most significant breaches of the territory’s border in years.

Rachid Sbihi, head of the association representing Guardia Civil officers in Ceuta, described the scenes as “absolute chaos” and said the border had “totally collapsed”. He said the event was a “humanitarian crisis”.

open image in gallery Many of the migrants have been sent back after the border breach ( AFP/Getty )

Spain has deployed police and military personnel to deal with the crisis and promised that those involved will be sent back to Morocco.

On Friday, authorities confirmed that half of the migrants had already returned, many of them voluntarily.

Moroccan forces used water cannons, batons and tear gas at the Ceuta gates to prevent more crowds storming the autonomous Spanish territory.

Mr Sanchez went on to blame gangs for the crisis, saying that they “deceive so many young people, and ultimately lead many of them to their deaths, whether in the ocean or, as in this case, at Spain’s border in the autonomous city of Ceuta”.

Right-wing leaders in Europe were quick to condemn the incident, urging tighter controls of EU borders.

open image in gallery Migrants sit on rocks after swimming through the waters close to the border with Morocco ( AFP/Getty )

open image in gallery Children were among the crowds trying to make it across the border ( AFP/Getty )

Ms Meloni said that the “striking” images confirmed that “uncontrolled illegal immigration poses a concrete threat to the security of Europe’s borders”.

“Italy will not stand by and watch,” she wrote. “We are convening the relevant bodies, and following these meetings, we are prepared to intervene with extraordinary measures to defend the borders and the safety of citizens, including the suspension of the Schengen area with Spain.

“On illegal immigration, we will not yield an inch: defending the borders, stopping human traffickers, and ensuring effective repatriations will continue to be the line of this government.”

open image in gallery Spain’s leader Pedro Sanchez has called the breach an attack on the country’s territorial integrity ( Reuters )

France’s far-right politician Marine Le Pen accused the Spanish government of “encouraging” the crisis.

“Faced with the massive and coordinated influx of migrants into Spain, encouraged by the Spanish government, France must without delay strengthen controls at its borders,” she wrote in a post on X.

“And in 2027, we will put an end to this madness by reserving Schengen free movement for EU nationals.”

President of the EU Commission Ursula von der Leyen called for the swift return of migrants to Morocco, while German chancellor Friedrich Merz said: “The protection of the EU’s external borders is crucial for combating illegal migration.

“I support Spain’s intention not to allow illegal migrants onto the European continent. The EU’s Return Directive must now be implemented without delay.”

The surge is reportedly linked to a recent ruling by Spain’s supreme court, which concluded that migrants intercepted at sea while attempting to reach Ceuta or Melilla cannot be deported or returned back under new rules. The decision does not apply to crossings by land.

Mr Sanchez said that the ruling had been misinterpreted.

“It appears that this interpretation of the Supreme Court’s ruling spread like wildfire over the past few hours through the networks of human trafficking organisations, triggering the kind of mass surge we witnessed yesterday,” he said.

Juan Jesus Vivas, mayor-president of Ceuta, called on the government to declare a national emergency. The interior ministry rejected the calls on the grounds that migration did not constitute a national emergency, but vowed to provide additional resources.

Opposition leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo described the situation as a “national security crisis” and urged the government to take stronger action.

A pilot has been rushed to the hospital after a US Marine Corps F-35B fighter jet crashed near a Southern California air base on Friday.

The pilot ejected from the F-35B before it crashed near the Miramar air base in San Diego, the US Marine Corps has confirmed. The advanced jet, valued at approximately $109 million, went down at about 10 a.m. local time.

The crash has been officially classified as a "Class A mishap" by the Marines.

"The pilot ejected, was transported to a local medical facility in stable condition for evaluation and treatment of non-life-threatening injuries,” the Marines Corps said.

open image in gallery The scene of the F-35 jet crash ( KGTV via AP )

open image in gallery The jet crashed near Marine Corps Air Station Miramar in San Diego ( Luke Johnson/The San Diego Union-Tribune via AP )

Aerial footage from a news helicopter captured a plume of black smoke rising from the wreckage in a dirt field. Multiple military and firefighting vehicles were visible at the scene, with what appeared to be white flame retardant covering the ground and personnel spraying the debris with a fire hose.

A witness described seeing the crash while driving on nearby Interstate 15 and said the aircraft flew over the freeway with its cockpit open before going down in "a big fireball." They reported seeing a parachute, presumably carrying the ejected pilot, floating down toward the ground.

The crash occurred near the flight line at the northern San Diego military station, according to 1st Lt. Blake Starbuck, a base spokesman.

The F-35B is a variant of the advanced stealth fighter jet utilized by the Marine Corps, Navy, and Air Force. This particular "B" version is engineered for short takeoffs and is capable of vertical landings, showcasing its unique operational flexibility.

Marine Corps Air Station Miramar, the location of the crash, famously hosted the Navy fighter pilot training school depicted in the original Top Gun film, earning it the moniker "Fightertown USA" during its prime.

The school later relocated to Naval Air Station Fallon in Nevada in 1996 after the base was transferred to the Marine Corps.

News.title: Battle rages over access to new ‘miracle’ HIV drug
News.content:
For the first time in the four-decade fight against HIV there is a “miracle” drug that can all but eliminate the risk of infection, but in the Latin American countries where it was tested almost no one can get it.

Trials show that Lenacapavir, made by Gilead Sciences, is almost 100 per cent effective in preventing HIV infection. With just two shots a year, those taking it will avoid contracting the virus even when frequently exposed.

The drug, which many believe could bring an end to the global HIV pandemic, costs $14,000 a dose in the United States. Gilead has agreed to licence generic versions of the pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) medication at around $60 a dose in 120 low-and middle-income countries, but almost all of Latin America is excluded.

Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru are among those with serious HIV epidemics that are shut out, despite having run some of the clinical trials that proved the drug works.

Their status as “upper-middle income countries” means they are too rich to qualify for the cut price generic version and yet they remain too poor to pay the US price.

News.title: Senior dating: a guide to finding love later in life
News.content:
Whether you’re a widow, widower or divorcee, the thought of online dating in later life can feel daunting. However, more and more people are turning to the internet to find romance. Roughly 16 per cent of UK adults are using online dating services to meet a partner, according to Statista. Among them, there are lots of singles over 50 using dating sites.

So here’s how to navigate your senior dating online, with expert advice from psychologist and dating coach Dr Pam Spurr, and sex and relationship coach Angela Vossen.

How do I know if I'm ready to date again as a senior?

Coming out of any relationship is hard. If you’re hoping to date after a divorce, bereavement or break up, it can take a long time to feel ready to date again. Dr Spurr advises taking your time.

“Many people feel bruised, even traumatised, after coming out of a long-term relationship or having been bereaved,” she explains. “Your feelings naturally vary from day to day about whether you're ready to get back out to look for love – or even for fun. A crucial factor is if you've come to the point where you have more good days compared to bad days”.

Dr Spurr explains that good days are the days on which you feel more optimistic about life generally, and you find your thoughts turning to meeting someone new. “That's an important sign that you are healing,” she says. “However, if you're still feeling deeply insecure or are riddled with self-doubt about your worthiness, take your time. When you feel worthy, you will find someone worthy of you”.

Feeling heartbroken? Learn how to get over a break up

How to start senior dating online

If you’re new to online dating, it can feel intimidating at first. The secret is taking things step by step so that you do things at your own pace. The first step, however, should be choosing a senior dating site that will help match you with like-minded people. This will narrow your search and ensure your dating experience is more successful.

Step 1: Create an online profile

Once you’ve decided on a dating site or app and signed up, you’ll be asked to write a dating profile. This should reflect who you are along with your passions, values and what you seek in a partner.

Try to be authentic rather than creating a fantasy version of yourself. If you exaggerate your accomplishments, your date will only feel deceived once they get to know you. Likewise, don’t be tempted to use a photo of yourself from 10 years ago.

What are you waiting for? |  Single and looking to find true love? Sign up today for Telegraph Dating and join more than 220,000 like-minded people. Join today

Step 2: Spark meaningful chats with potential dates

Once you have signed up to a senior dating site and created a profile, you will be free to start looking at other people’s profiles and sending messages to anyone that catches your attention. But how can you initiate a conversation after an introduction?

“When messaging people on dating sites, ask open-ended questions to spark meaningful chats,” says Angela. A good example would be, ‘I can see you enjoy travel. What place have you always wanted to visit but haven’t yet?’ or “tell me more about your love of tennis? Did you watch the US Open?” If things go really well and the chat seems to flow naturally, you may decide to organise a phone chat or ask them out on a date. An initial chat over the phone can help gauge how well you get on and how easily the conversation flows. If this goes well, meeting in person may feel less nerve wracking and a little less ‘blind’.

Step 3: Prioritise your safety

“While most people are well intentioned online, it’s important to protect your safety,” advises Ms Vossen. “Keep personal details private (like where you live or your social media profiles) until you’ve met in person and built trust”. You should also arrange first dates in public places, share your plans with a friend, and trust your instincts if something feels off.

If the first date or two doesn’t quite hit the mark, try not to be too disappointed and remember that you can say no to another date. Ms Vossen says: “Be patient – online dating takes time, but with practice, you’ll gain confidence and enjoy the journey”.

Traditional ways to meet senior singles

Of course, couples continue to meet in a manner that predates online dating sites. If you’re keen to join the older dating scene but find the online world overwhelming, there are plenty of ways to meet people in real life.

1. Holidays and group trips

We are often our best selves on holiday, so it’s the ideal place to find a single senior woman or to meet men if the opportunity presents itself. Why not organise a trip on which you meet new people while doing what you love, whether that’s cycling, walking, sightseeing or just travelling around a new part of the world. There are many escorted tours that cater to specific age groups and interests. They also take away the stress of organising a trip yourself.

“An organised holiday or trip can be a great place to meet someone new and there are many organisations offering these for the over 50s,” says Dr Spur. “A word of caution though, you can spend a lot of money and there's no guarantee that you will meet that special person. However, if it's a place you've wanted to travel to then go with the mindset that you're going to have a great trip. If you meet someone, that's an added bonus”.

2. Activities and social groups

Whether you enjoy walking, reading or volunteering, taking up a new hobby or joining a social group is a great way to enhance your social life and increase your chances of meeting a new romantic interest.

“Joining a club or taking up a hobby can be a fantastic way of meeting singles who enjoy the same pastimes,” says Dr Spur. “You're doing an activity you enjoy knowing that there might also be someone there that will catch your eye”.

If you do meet someone that you’re interested in at a social event, Dr Spur advises starting with a simple ‘hello’ and an easy question such as how long they've been doing that particular activity or hobby. “This can open-up a friendly conversation that might lead to flirting down the line,” she says.

Start online dating for seniors today

Whichever way you decide to start looking for love, approach it in a way that you feel comfortable with. Signing up to an online dating service is a great way to meet other seniors. Remember, it’s never too late to begin a new chapter.

News.title: UK economy to flatline, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Britain’s economy is set to almost grind to a halt for the rest of the year, the Bank of England has warned.

Growth will drop to just 0.1pc per quarter, the Bank predicted, slowing sharply after a strong start to 2026.

Higher petrol prices and energy bills, a weak jobs market and rising mortgage costs are all draining confidence and spending power from the economy.

Inflation, which slowed to a 15-month low of 2.6pc in June, is also expected to rise again to 3.2pc later this year, the Bank warned.

Andrew Bailey, the Bank’s Governor, said inflation had “fallen faster than we’d expected” but warned that war in the Middle East would lead to a fresh spike.

He added that growth would “weaken slightly further in the near term as the effects of the conflict weigh further on demand”.

The Bank also predicted that unemployment will rise back above 5pc in the coming months, limiting workers’ ability to ask for higher wages to cope with rising living costs.

It presents a challenging backdrop for Andy Burnham and his Chancellor, John Healey, who have pledged to help voters struggling with the cost of living.

The forecasts came as policymakers led by Mr Bailey held interest rates at 3.75pc.

Although three members of the nine-strong Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted for higher rates, up from two at the previous meeting, the Governor dismissed suggestions the Bank is moving towards higher interest rates.

The public should “not… [think] the Bank of England is edging towards a hike,” Mr Bailey said.

“Frankly there is nothing I have said, or any of us have said, along those lines. We took a decision today to leave the Bank Rate unchanged and that is the relevant conclusion.”

Clare Lombardelli, a Deputy Governor, said voting to keep rates at 3.75pc “was not a close judgement”, calling the decision “pretty clear” given slowing inflation in the domestic economy.

Officials are monitoring the economy for any signs that increases in oil, gas and petrol prices caused by the war in Iran are creeping into higher costs and wages in the wider economy.

Mr Bailey said: “The possibility of repeated resumptions of conflict, combined with lower than usual European gas stock levels and a fall in global refining output, mean that risks to energy prices lie to the upside.”

He added: “Reassuringly, there are few signs so far that second-round effects are generating more broad-based inflationary pressures.”

Companies are struggling to pass higher costs on to their customers because of the economy’s weakness, he added.

Workers are typically securing only modest pay rises as the weak jobs market leaves them in a poor position to push for bigger salaries.

Mr Bailey stressed there are still major risks to the outlook given the war and promised to “monitor the situation carefully” and was “ready to adjust our stance”.

“It is our job to ensure that inflation gets back to the 2pc target and stays there, and that is what we will do,” he said.

Borrowing costs dropped in financial markets after the decision.

The Government’s two-year borrowing cost fell from 4.44pc to 4.34pc, the sharpest fall in a month.

The FTSE 250 index of mid-sized UK companies rose 0.8pc to a record high of 24,184.10.

Traders still believe the Bank will raise interest rates twice within a year.

However, Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said rate rises “remain more a threat than a reality”.

He said there was evidence of disinflation in the economy and interest rates could be “cut to 3pc in 2027”, adding: “That’s very different to market pricing for rates to be close to 4.5pc in 2027.”

News.title: Arsonists torch more Ebola clinics as misinformation spirals in DRC
News.content:
Two more Ebola treatment facilities have reportedly been burned down in recent days as health officials struggle to overcome violent public mistrust of medical teams.

At least a dozen facilities have now been attacked since Congo declared its Ebola outbreak amid fear, misinformation and suspicion of outside authorities.

The outbreak is the fastest growing on record and officials said the virus had now killed more than 1,500 people.

The official death toll from the outbreak centred on the north eastern Ituri province of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen by 500 in only a week.

Sources told the Telegraph the large jump in deaths was largely caused by a “data harmonisation exercise” between different regions, and the new deaths may not have all happened in the past week.

However, the daily confirmed toll has also continued to climb sharply with the latest government update reporting 50 people dying in the previous 24 hours.

Airfinity, a health analytics firm, said the outbreak “continues to outpace detection and the response” and there is a high chance of it spreading further inside DRC.

News.title: Race for vaccine against new Ebola strain gets $8.5m boost
News.content:
The “most promising” vaccine to tackle the Ebola strain behind an explosive outbreak in the Congo has been given an $8.5 million boost, as researchers race to develop an effective shot.

So far at least 3,360 people have been infected and 1,487 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in an epidemic triggered by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola.

But unlike past outbreaks of the more common Zaire strain, there are currently no approved vaccines to tackle Bundibugyo.

On Thursday, the Coalition of Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi) revealed up to $8.5 million of funding for the only single-dose inoculation, which was described as the “most promising vaccine candidate” by the World Health Organization (WHO) in an analysis in May.

It is being developed by researchers at Hilleman Laboratories – a unique partnership between the pharmaceutical giant Merck and the British philanthropic powerhouse Wellcome, which is headquartered in Singapore.

The vaccine candidate is a Bundibugyo version of the Ervebo shot, which was created by Merck (MSD in Europe) and has already been approved for Ebola Zaire.

It uses a rVSV platform, where a modified version of VSV virus is used to train the immune system to react to target pathogens – in this instance, the Bundibugyo species replaces Zaire.

News.title: AMR chatbot could prevent drug-resistant infections in African hospitals
News.content:
A phone-based chatbot advising medics how to prescribe antibiotics has helped raise the quality of care in African hospitals and should stop bugs developing dangerous resistance, developers say.

Staff at four hospitals across Zambia and Kenya have been using two digital tools in a pilot project to try to address one of the world’s biggest health threats.

Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is caused by germs evolving so that medicines such as antibiotics designed to kill them no longer work.

The menace is linked to nearly five million deaths each year and makes it increasingly difficult to treat infections. The annual death toll could nearly double in the next 25 years, according to some forecasts.

The rise in AMR is being significantly driven by the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in human medicine and in agriculture.

Using antibiotics when they are not necessary, using the wrong ones, or getting the dosage wrong, all add to the chances that bugs will develop resistance.

With a shortage of new drugs in the development pipeline, one push to defeat AMR has been to get medics to stick to existing prescription, dosage and treatment advice.

The Antibiotic Stewardship Programme through Innovation, Research, and Education (ASPIRE) is trying to give them guidance using technology they already have in their pockets.

News.title: Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC
News.content:
Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at this year’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, following on from her third place at the 2018 Games in Australia.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes shares emotional Eddie Howe message after Newcastle exit
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes shares emotional Eddie Howe message after Newcastle exit

Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes has paid an emotional tribute to Eddie Howe after his departure from St James' Park was confirmed

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes has sent an emotional message to Eddie Howe after his Newcastle departure was confirmed. (Image: Chronicle Live)

Arsenal transfer target Bruno Guimaraes has paid tribute to Eddie Howe, hailing him as the "King of the club" in a heartfelt message to the departing Newcastle United head coach following confirmation of his exit. The club confirmed Howe's departure earlier today after five years at the helm.

‌



It's another bitter blow for the Magpies during yet another summer of upheaval. Supporters had hoped for a calmer summer interlude than last year, with Alexander Isak's transfer saga dominating the headlines and causing unrest at St. James' Park.

Fast forward 12 months, and the picture looks just as bleak. Newcastle have sold Anthony Gordon to Barcelona, Sandro Tonali to Tottenham Hotspur and are at risk of losing captain, Guimaraes, to Arsenal.

‌



A 4-1 defeat to Bristol City in pre-season was the final act under Howe's tenure, a game in which Guimaraes missed as a result of an extended holiday. The 28-year-old has now taken to social media to share a heartfelt tribute to Howe, which read: "King of this club!

Bruno Guimaraes pushes for Arsenal transfer with Newcastle agreement imminent READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"Thanks for everything you've done for us. I loved our time together. You made me a better player and person. No words can say how much I enjoyed being your player. Wish you all the very best in your future gaffer."

‌



In another post, Guimaraes added: "Ed, how could I ever put into words how grateful I am to you? First of all, I want to thank you for bringing me to this club. Thank you for everything you've done for me, for helping me grow not only as a player, but more importantly, as a person.

We can't control the forces that are at play here, we've just got to make sure that when Bruno comes back, we look after him and he trains well, which I'm sure he will do. And he makes a difference as he always has done.

Article continues below

"We've spoken numerous times. Assurances? I don't think you can push too hard for those. I've said many times we want players who are committed, and Bruno has always been committed. His training performances and his game performances have been outstanding, every time he's worn the shirt, he's played with the fans by his side. I'd love to see that continue."

Sports.content:
Chelsea and FA drop Mykhailo Mudryk statement

Mykhailo Mudryk will now be available to play for Chelsea. A statement from the FA confirmed the news, saying: "The FA can confirm that the anti-doping disciplinary proceedings against Mykhailo Mudryk were resolved with the agreement of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) on 30 July 2026.

"In the context of that agreement, Mr Mudryk has accepted his commission of Anti-Doping Rule Violations (ADRVs) and accepted a period of ineligibility. On 22 October 2024, Mr Mudryk was subject to an out-of-competition doping control, which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance.

"The FA notified Mr Mudryk of that finding on 4 December 2024 and imposed a provisional suspension. On 23 May 2025, The FA charged Mr Mudryk with ADRVs in breach of Regulations 3 and 4 of its 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

"On 7 to 9 January 2026, a hearing took place before an independent Regulatory Commission. The Regulatory Commission found that Mr Mudryk had committed the charged ADRVs and imposed a four-year period of ineligibility. Subsequently, Mr Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

"Since then, changes have been made to WADA Technical Document (TD2027MRL) which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk's sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no ADRVs would have resulted.

"Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, The FA and Mr Mudryk have now - with the agreement of WADA - resolved the appeal proceedings in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the World Anti-Doping Code and Regulation 90 of the 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

"As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the Anti-Doping Rule Violations charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement. Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect."

Chelsea also uploaded their own statement which said: "Chelsea FC acknowledges today's announcement by The Football Association confirming the resolution of the anti-doping proceedings involving Mykhailo Mudryk.

"From the outset, this has been an extremely difficult period for Misha, both professionally and personally, and we are pleased that the matter has now reached a conclusion which allows him to return to football with immediate effect.

"We have always supported Misha throughout this process while fully respecting the integrity of the anti-doping system and the legal process. We welcome the acknowledgement that advances in the applicable scientific reporting standards for more reliable testing mean that, had Misha's sample been analysed under today's technical requirements, it would not have been reported as a positive test and no anti-doping rule violation would have resulted.

"That is an important part of the context surrounding the agreed resolution and allows everyone involved to move forward. "Misha has consistently maintained that he never knowingly or intentionally used a prohibited substance and did not know how traces of the substance entered his system. Throughout this process he has conducted himself professionally and with resilience during what has undoubtedly been one of the most challenging periods of his career.

"We know how much this opportunity to return means to him. Our focus now is on supporting Misha’s reintegration into the squad and helping him resume his career. Chelsea FC remains fully committed to the highest standards of sporting integrity and compliance with all anti-doping regulations. Everyone at the Club now looks forward to helping Misha return to full fitness, back into the squad and back onto the pitch."

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford has chance to 'hurt' Man Utd as two transfer moves proposed
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford has chance to 'hurt' Man Utd as two transfer moves proposed

Marcus Rashford is a Manchester United player on paper, but he has been widely expected to leave the Reds in the transfer window

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford is still facing an uncertain summer (Image: Icon Sportswire, Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Manchester United have been warned not to sell Marcus Rashford to a Premier League rival. Rene Meulensteen, who was Sir Alex Ferguson's assistant manager at Old Trafford. He believes selling Rashford to the likes of Tottenham Hotspur could hurt the club.

‌



Spurs were recently linked with a £30million move for the England international, whose future at the club is uncertain. Barcelona chose not to sign him permanently, and no club has yet come forward with a meaningful offer for the Reds.

‌



Michael Carrick re-integrating him back into the squad is not impossible, but it's widely been believed both parties feel a clean break is best for everyone. If this is the case, Meulenseteen warned United not to sell to a Premier League rival.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Speaking to Andy's Bet Club, Meulensteen, when questioned whether the scenario might mirror United's choice to sell Scott McTominay, who has since flourished for Napoli, responded: "Would selling Marcus Rashford be a repeat of selling Scott McTominay?

"I don't think people see Scott McTominay the same way. He moved because the club wanted to sell, and he has done brilliantly since. People might wonder if United sold him too early.

‌



"But selling Marcus Rashford to a direct competitor like Arsenal or Chelsea could really hurt you. He is still a player who can make a difference. Ideally, if United sell him, they should sell him abroad."

View 3 Images Barcelona chose not to sign Rashford permanently (Image: Aitor Alcalde Colomer, Getty Images)

Meulensteen also suggested Saudi Arabia could be a potential destination or maybe even the MLS, saying: "Saudi Arabia could be an option for Rashford depending on what he wants," before adding: "Perhaps one of the other big clubs will sign him so he can keep playing in the Champions League. Or he might make a move to Saudi or maybe the MLS, who knows?"

‌



Meulensteen also urged Carrick to open up a dialogue with Rashford to gauge his state of mind and establish how he might contribute to the club. He said: "Michael Carrick is the type of person who recognises Marcus's qualities.

"They need an open conversation so Marcus understands what is required. Michael Carrick won't want to bring someone back if it creates another problem. If the clarity is there, he would be happy to bring him back into the fold.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick still has many options this summer (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



"However, with the other players available, there wouldn't be a guaranteed start every week. The fact that it is taking so long to find clarity suggests there is still something brewing in the background. If all parties were happy for him to come back, they would likely have made that clear very quickly."

When it comes to attacking options, United's primary weapons are Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko and Amad Diallo, with Bruno Fernandes and Mason Mount frequently operating in the pocket just behind the striker.

Patrick Dorgu was also reinvented as a left-winger under Carrick, chipping in with several crucial goals before an injury derailed his progress last season. United still have further pre-season friendlies remaining on the schedule.

The FIFA President is facing increasing pressure over his handling of the US tournament. FIFA claimed in its latest statement that its plan to sell off a stake in the World Cup "was disrupted by incorrect media reports".

‌



But that cut no ice with the English FA, European nations and the Asian Football Confederation. It is yet another controversy on a long list for the Swiss born football chief.

‌



Ironically, he was hailed as the organisation's saviour when he was appointed 10 years ago.

View 4 Images The FIFA President is facing increasing pressure over his handling of the US tournament and his relationship with President Donald Trump (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Gianni Infantino gets fresh reality check as World Cup boycott grows amid calls for change READ MORE :

Infantino's unlikely route to sporting power began in the small Swiss town of Brig, an Alpine transport hub for nearby ski resorts. As a ginger, freckle-faced youngster, he became president of his local amateur club, FC Brig-Glis, on the mandate that his mother would wash the team's kits. It was the shape of things to come. He is a pragmatist who 'likes to get things done,' according to football insiders.

‌



And that means getting alongside everyone from President Putin - he collected a Russian Order of Friendship from him after the 2018 World Cup - to President Trump, who calls Infantino 'The King of Soccer'.

Born in Switzerland to Italian parents, Infantino is fluent in French, German, Italian, Arabic, English, Portuguese and Spanish. He added Lebanese citizenship to his passport collection under special rules for high-profile figures.

View 4 Images The FIFA President Gianni Infantino with President Donald Trump in the Oval Office (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



His wife and the mother of his four children, Lina al-Ashkar, is Lebanese.

His steady rise started at UEFA in 2000, where he worked in the legal department before becoming deputy general secretary in 2007 and then secretary general in 2009.

After Michel Platini was undone by scandal, Infantino, his former right hand man, was thrust forward for the role. He started his tenure with a low profile, flying to one early meeting on EasyJet.

‌



At this summer's World Cup, he crisscrossed countries on a Qatar Airways private jet.

He pledged to rid football of its reputation for greed and corruption, while looking after UEFA's interests. UEFA backed Infantino with £438,000 to support his campaign.

Ten years on, few of his supporters in European football remain.

‌



FIFA stressed: "Nobody is selling football. This is not something we would ever entertain." But the sky-high prices for the US tournament, Infantino's bizarre award of a 'peace prize' to Trump and now the links to Trump's family in the private investment World Cup plan may signal the end of his tenure. The plans to sell stakes in the tournament to private investors for $20m (£15m) are hugely unpopular. Infantino claims it is about “the democratisation of football worldwide”. But the investor group for FFE would be led by Thrive Eternal.

It was founded earlier this year by Joshua Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump ’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.

That has already led to accusations from Democrat Congressman Jamie Raskin that FIFA is “going into business” with the Trump family.

‌



View 4 Images The FIFA HQ in Zurich (Image: Getty Images)

Infantino became Fifa president in 2016 when he beat Asian Football Confederation president Sheikh Salman al-Khalifa by 115 votes to 88. He was due to stand for a fourth term in March.

It had been anticipated he would be re-elected unopposed before the World Cup plan which critics claim 'sells the soul of football'.

‌



Associations around the world had already confirmed their intention to support the 56-year-old. But Concacaf members are losing faith in Infantino.

Nasser Al-Khelaifi, President of Champions League winners Paris St-Germain, is already being touted as his successor.

Former Uefa chief executive Lars-Christer Olsson told the BBC that Infantino has overplayed his hand and his position could be in trouble. When asked if Infantino should be removed from his role, Olsson said: "I think that should be a new start for football."

‌



View 4 Images The FIFA President is facing increasing pressure over his handling of the US tournament (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Infantino opened the Qatar World Cup by saying: "Today I have strong feelings. Today I feel Qatari, I feel Arab, I feel African, I feel gay, I feel disabled, I feel a migrant worker." A total of 6,500 migrant workers from India, Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka had reportedly died in Qatar since it won its World Cup bid. Infantino added: "We have been taught many lessons by Europeans and the Western world. I am European. For what we have been doing for 3,000 years, we should be apologising for the next 3,000 years before giving moral lessons." Fans around the world criticised his speech. Plans to stage the 2030 World Cup across three continents - Africa, Europe and South America - and the 2034 tournament in Saudi Arabia attracted yet more controversy. Norway's football federation abstained from the process and argued the bidding process undermined "Fifa's reforms for good governance" and challenged "trust in Fifa". In May 2024, it was revealed Infantino received a 33% pay rise, - determined by an independent committee - upon his re-election the previous year. It took his base salary from 1.95m Swiss francs (£1.7m) in 2022 to 2.6m Swiss francs (£2.3m). On top of that, he was due an unchanged bonus of 1.65m Swiss francs (£1.5m).

Infantino, who was earning about £1.3m when first elected in 2016, is now close to Blatter's final annual salary. Infantino handed Trump the controversial FIFA Peace Prize. Within a week came the announcement of high ticket prices for the finals. Then he had to apologise after saying it was "really special" no British nationals were arrested during the 2022 World Cup. His relationship with Trump was thrust into the spotlight when the US President asked FIFA to overturn Folarin Balogun's one-match suspension. USA forward Balogun was sent off during the last-32 tie against Bosnia-Herzegovina but was cleared to feature in the next round after an unprecedented intervention from Trump, which drew widespread criticism. Infantino has offered all 211 of FIFA's member associations $40m (£30m) if they back his controversial plans to sell stakes in the organisation's major competitions - including the World Cup. After being re-elected unopposed in 2019 and 2023, he is approaching another election year in 2027.

Article continues below

Infantino will be able to stand again, even though FIFA statutes limit the president to a maximum of three terms.

His future is on a knife edge though Asia and Africa, the two regions that have benefited from the hugely increased finances, hold almost half of the votes.

Sports.title: Piers Morgan makes Gianni Infantino U-turn as he admits 'I was wrong'
Sports.content:
Piers Morgan makes Gianni Infantino U-turn as he admits 'I was wrong'

FIFA President Gianni Infantino has come under serious criticism for his plan to sell a share in the World Cup to private investors and Piers Morgan has issued his thoughts

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has been at the centre of controversy once again (Image: Getty Images)

Piers Morgan has called for Gianni Infantino to leave in the midst of his World Cup sale scandal. The FIFA President has found himself at the centre of controversy over the past few weeks, having launched an idea that will see a share of the World Cup sold off to foreign investors.

‌



That plot has not gone down well across the globe, with UEFA, CONCACAF and more federations slamming the plan. The organisers of the European game have also threatened to pull their nations out of any future FIFA competitions should they go through with the plan.

‌



Broadcaster Morgan is among those to have spoken out in opposition and claimed that it is now time for Infantino to step aside.

‌



Taking to social media, he wrote: “I thought FIFA boss Gianni Infantino was a force for good in football. I was wrong. The shameful Balogun fiasco was bad enough, but his greedy, tawdry attempt to flog off the World Cup is beyond the pale. He must go.”

Gianni Infantino ally quits as FIFA boss blasted over World Cup plans in angry statement READ MORE :

Morgan is not the only one to have suggested that Morgan needs to leave his role as FIFA president. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham also questioned his suitability for the job after his World Cup plan was unveiled.

He said: “This was an outrageous suggestion. The idea that it could even be brought forward shows that, in my view, [he] is the wrong man to lead the organisation."

‌



Those comments came after Burnham tore into Infantino’s plan to sell a share in the World Cup. Talking to social media, he said: “Let me say this very directly. Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine.

“The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone's to sell. Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out. Football belongs to the fans. It always has, and it always will.”

View 2 Images FIFA's plan to sell a share of the World Cup has been widely criticised (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The fallout from FIFA’s proposal has even worsened over the past couple of days, with Infantino’s senior advisor, Carlos Cordeiro, choosing to resign from his position.

A statement read: "As a Senior Advisor to the FIFA President, a former banker, and a lifelong football fan, I cannot stand by while FIFA considers selling a stake in the World Cup. Let me be clear: I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally. It is a bad deal for FIFA's Member Associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game.

"Football has been central to my life, and after more than 35 years in banking, I understand both the value of this asset and the consequences of giving part of it away. That is why this proposal should be rejected. FIFA already has access to extraordinary financial resources.

‌



"This proposal has become a defining question for FIFA's future. After careful consideration, I can no longer continue in my role as Senior Advisor to the FIFA President. I have therefore resigned with immediate effect. FIFA's responsibility is not to maximise commercial returns at any cost. It is to protect and strengthen football for future generations. When those principles come into conflict, football must come first.

"It has been the privilege of a lifetime to serve FIFA for more than five years and to work alongside dedicated, principled people who care deeply about the game. I hope they, too, will speak up, because decisions of this magnitude should be made in the interests of football, not those who stand to profit from it."

Sports.title: FIFA chief accuses Gianni Infantino of DECEIVING staff over World Cup plot - 'If I lose my job so be it'
Sports.content:
FIFA chief accuses Gianni Infantino of DECEIVING staff over World Cup plot - 'If I lose my job so be it'

The FIFA president, Gianni Infantino, has come under significant fire over plans to sell stakes in FIFA tournaments such as the World Cup to private investors

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has been accused of 'deceiving' staff with his World Cup sale plot (Image: GSI/Icon Sport via Getty Images)

The chief operating officer of FIFA has accused Gianni Infantino of 'deceiving' staff in relation to the plot to sell World Cup stakes to private investors, adding the proposal 'must not go ahead'.

‌



Infantino unveiled plans to sell off a portion of FIFA's commercial businesses, including tournaments such as the World Cup and the Club World Cup, to private investors. However, his proposal has been met with a ferocious backlash from football's other governing bodies including UEFA, whose nations are ready to boycott future World Cups if the plans go ahead.

‌



One of the 56-year-old's senior advisors, Carlos Cordeiro, has already resigned over the plans. And now another of Infantino's colleagues has torn into the proposal.

‌



Kevin Lamour, who has been FIFA's COO since 2024, says Infantino “deceived” staff with his scheme in a damning statement shared with AP, saying they “deserve better than contempt and intimidation.”

Gianni Infantino ally quits as FIFA boss blasted over World Cup plans in angry statement READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino gets fresh reality check as World Cup boycott grows amid calls for change READ MORE :

“It is the project of one person,” Lamour said. “Not only must this project not go ahead … but the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions.”

Lamour, who also worked with Infantino at UEFA previously, did not resign from his post like Cordeiro but added: “And if that means I lose my job, then so be it. I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.”

‌



View 2 Images FIFA COO Kevin Lamour has hit out at Infantino and his plans

His comments come hot on the heels of Cordeiro deciding to resign from his post over the plans, which prompted UEFA to confirm their nations will boycott future tournaments if they go ahead.

“I cannot stand by while FIFA considers selling a stake in the World Cup,” Cordeiro said.

Article continues below

“Let me be clear. I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally,” he added, describing the proposed $20 billion commercial subsidiary as a “bad deal for football”.

Sports.title: American Affair flies the flag for Goldie at Goodwood
Sports.content:
Scottish speedball American Affair bounced back to form to claim top honours in the King George Qatar Stakes at Goodwood.

Jim Goldie's stable star won the King Charles III Stakes at Royal Ascot last summer, but missed the remainder of the 2025 season through injury.

A second-place finish behind the reopposing Night Raider in Haydock's Temple Stakes in May suggested he retained a good level of his ability, but having trailed home last of all when defending his Ascot title and since come up short in a Listed race at York, he was a 12-1 shot for his latest Group Two assignment.

Always up with the pace in the group that raced closest to the stands rail, American Affair finished off strongly in the hands of his regular partner Paul Mulrennan to get up and beat Rumstar and Time For Sandals down the middle of the track, with Australian raider Asfoora running her best race for a while in fourth.

Goldie senior stayed closer to home, but his son, George, said: "My dad is at Musselburgh, we couldn't both come here, but I think he'll be sorry to have missed out!

"My daughter rides him every day, he's a lovely-natured horse and he's obviously very talented.

"We had faith he'd be back to this level, we've been happy with him at home but things were interrupted by the injury he had at the back end of last year.

"This year it has been a case of building him back up to his best, he showed a glimmer at Haydock three runs ago, but Ascot was a bit of a disaster - he just pulled too hard.

"He ran well at York when he was drawn badly, so we were coming here very hopeful. He's been getting back into that flow of racing properly and finishing his race off.

"We were hoping today was going to suit him better, we were coming here very hopeful."

On future plans, he added: "The plan is to go for the Nunthorpe now, then maybe the Curragh or he could go up to six (furlongs) for the Haydock Sprint Cup.

"We've not entered him in the Abbaye, the Flying Five at the Curragh after the Nunthorpe is more likely."

Weighing-room stalwart Mulrennan said: "He's done everything right today so, touch wood, he comes back from this good. We'll enjoy today, but we've got the Nunthorpe and possibly America would be nice.

"At this stage of the game I've probably got more years behind me than in front of me, but I feel I'm still going strong. It's very competitive, it's hard. I've only got one ride down here this week, but we've made it count.

"I've got my driver with me, Adele (wife). The last time I won it was on Moviesta, Adele drove me then. I've won this race twice and I probably should have won it twice again - Easton Angel probably should have won and Moviesta another year was unlucky, so it's been an unlucky race for me and a lucky race for me, but we got it right today."

Wendy McGrandles of Barraston Racing, who own American Affair with Goldie, said: "He's had one or two excuses and we always felt that he was as good as he was last year. It's once in a lifetime for us, small breeders.

"I remember him as a foal and thinking we could maybe send him eventing if he wasn't fast enough to go racing. He was broken in to go eventing because we weren't sure whether he would be big enough or fast enough to be a racehorse. He can always do that as a second career!"

Burke eyes American trip for Shayem after Thoroughbred success

Karl Burke is eyeing a trip to America with Shayem after he denied the fast-finishing favourite Talk Of New York in the HKJC World Pool Thoroughbred Stakes.

Having finished third behind Wednesday's Sussex Stakes one-two Bow Echo and Gstaad in the St James's Palace at Royal Ascot, this Group Three contest looked a gilt-edged opportunity for Charlie Appleby's Talk Of New York to get back on the winning trail and he was priced up accordingly as the 2-5 market leader.

But while his stablemate Catullus was deployed in a pacemaking role in an attempt to ensure a sound gallop, the favourite was still keen during the early exchanges under William Buick and it then took him a while to find top gear once asked to close the gap.

Karl Burke's Shayem - winner of the Listed Sir Henry Cecil Stakes at Newmarket three weeks ago - was always in the prime position behind Catullus and after grabbing the lead racing inside the final half-furlong, he had enough in hand to keep Talk Of New York at bay by half a length in the hands of Clifford Lee.

"We don't have to lead, but we knew Billy (Loughnane, riding Catullus) was going to go off a nice gallop and Cliff was the only one really to keep tabs on the leader," said Burke.

"Last year, you would have said that he was a soft ground horse but he has proven otherwise this year. We had no qualms about the ground or the track as he handled the undulations at Newmarket well.

"Cliff is very good with his fractions. It was a great performance and Abdulrazaq (Mohamdi, owner) will be delighted as he's a homebred horse as well. He's a great supporter of ours from Dubai.

"There is a nice race at Kentucky Downs for him in September and one at Colonial Downs as well. I don't think they are Grade Ones but they are very valuable races and if if we don't go there, we could come back for the Celebration Mile."

Appleby will let the dust settle on Talk Of New York's disappointing defeat before considering his next move.

He said: "At the top of the hill I thought they'd have to go a bit to go past the lead horse because he's no mug and he likes the track. Stretching to the mile was always going to be the undoing of Catullus - stop the clock a furlong out and we were a comfortable winner.

"William said himself, the front two stole a good march on him and they're two sensible horses. We knew that Catullus was not going to see the mile out eventually but Will said 'I was only just getting rolling there the last furlong'

"I'm not using the track as an excuse, I think the winner is sensible and is improving, he's done everything right, got a nice lead from us and used it, and we've gone and finished the race off.

"You could say do we need to step up in trip? Possibly. But he has got to learn to settle a little bit as well - that first furlong he does want to be a little bit aggressive, but I don't think that was really the undoing of the race to be fair. The pace was on and they weren't coming back at the end of the day."

Sports.title: Doyle: Owen can Dream big in the Stewards' Cup
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing ambassador Hollie Doyle reveals her thoughts on the big handicap of the day on Saturday, the Stewards’ Cup at Goodwood.

Dream chance for Owen in Stewards' Cup

Twenty-eight runners rampaging down the hill at Goodwood in one of the most famous handicaps in world racing is a sight to savour and this weekend's Coral Stewards' Cup Handicap (3.35) certainly lives up to expectations.

It's anyone's race but I cannot get away from James Owen's likely favourite Far Above Dream who has the form, the track experience, and the draw in his favour. The four-year-old ran a career-best to finish a close fourth in the Wokingham, just behind his talented stable mate Soldier's Tree, after scoring over this course and distance in May.

He has progressed up the handicap but can race off the same mark as he did at The Royal Meeting and can prove his liking for the cut and thrust of a big field handicap for an upwardly mobile trainer.

All-Weather winner has solid course form

Another on my shortlist for the Stewards' Cup is Ollie Sangster's Tuco Salamanca - an exciting ride for young Irish ace Dylan Browne-McMonagle.

Though his recent wins have been achieved on the All-Weather, including in good company at Newcastle last month, he does have solid course form to his name and has a handy middle draw.

In last weekend's blog I put up Charles Hills's lightly raced seven-year-old Mitbaahy as my 'Hot Shot' so won't be surprised if he makes the frame at big odds on the back of that second in the Group Three Hackwood Stakes at Newbury.

Star to deny Waardah a second win in Langtry

Santorini Star has the class and the constitution to add the Group Two Qatar Lillie Langtry Stakes (3.00) on Saturday to her Group Two victories in the Park Hill Stakes at Doncaster and the Jockey Club Stakes at Newmarket.

William Haggas's five-year-old had a rare blip in the Hardwicke Stakes at Royal Ascot but this is an ideal assignment for a mare who stays well and, crucially, has winning form at the track.

Her closest market rival will be the Owen Burrows-trained Waardah, who won this race last year and found only subsequent Group One Pretty Polly Stakes Winner Estrange too good in a Group Three at Carlisle last time. She is entitled to come on for her first outing since last Autumn, but Santorini Star's overall profile is more compelling.

Three in a row for veteran Al Aasy

William Haggas holds the key to the Group Three Coral Glorious Stakes (2.25) on Saturday with market leaders Al Aasy and Opportunity, but I am expecting the veteran to win this race for the third year in a row.

Tom (Marquand) will be looking to smuggle him into the race, just as Jim Crowley did 12 months ago, and can expect another committed performance from Shadwell's wonderful Sea The Stars gelding.

Seemingly as good as ever and proven on the track, he can get the better of Wathnan Racing's Duke Of Edinburgh Stakes hero Opportunity who took his form to a new level at Royal Ascot but needs to find more on this step back into Group company.

O'Brien gelding can build on Royal Ascot form

Godolphin's Valedictory will be well supported in the Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (1.50) on Saturday, and rightly so, but I am taking him on with Irish raider Aeronautic, who can improve on his third in the race last year.

Joseph O'Brien's five-year-old struck me as a winner waiting to happen when finishing fourth in the Copper Horse Stakes at the Royal Meeting. He hasn't won for a long time but has proven he can be highly competitive off this mark of 97.

Valedictory won over course and distance in May when he was transformed by the cheekpieces but a three-pound rise for a narrow win at Newmarket last time demands more from John and Thady Gosden's gelding.

Another to consider is Charlie Johnston's Northumberland Plate Victor Align The Stars who took this prize two years ago but has never won off a triple digit rating.

Time for talented Jack to shine

Promising apprentice Jack Nicholls can make a name for himself in the Phase Eight Handicap (4.10) on Saturday when he partners Naval Light for his in-form boss Karl Burke.

The three-year-old carries a relatively low weight and Jack's three-pound claim can give him a decisive edge in this higher grade following wins at Pontefract and Catterick this summer.

Startled has been running well for Richard Hughes who has enlisted another talented claimer in Harry Vigors for this assignment. He looks fairly treated on his course and distance second in May so should be in the mix.

Billy was just brilliant on stunning Echo

Bow Echo produced the performance of the week at the Qatar Goodwood Festival, showing a blistering turn of foot to win the Group One Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes (4.10, Wednesday) and extend his unbeaten record to six.

He's clearly a very special talent - a comment that applies to his young jockey Billy Loughnane, who has shown a maturity beyond his years on George Boughey's superstar.

It takes a special horse to get out of the kind of difficult situation he found himself in on the Downs but a top-class jockey to execute a victory as Billy did so coolly. It was a great ride that will live long in the memory of racing fans and one I thoroughly enjoyed watching.

Oxygen chamber is helping my recovery

Since coming out of hospital following my fall in May, I've been using a hyperbaric oxygen chamber which we've had installed at home, and the results are encouraging.

The chamber basically increases air pressure to deliver pure one hundred per cent oxygen into your bloodstream which helps with healing. Sitting in there for an hour a day has become part of my rehabilitation routine now.

I'm also continuing with my gym programme and physiotherapy at Oaksey House in Lambourn five days a week but still don't have any idea of a comeback date at this stage.

Sports.title: Newcastle to appoint Jaissle as new boss tomorrow after Howe exit confirmed
Sports.content:
Newcastle are set to announce Matthias Jaissle as their new head coach on Saturday after Eddie Howe's exit was confirmed.

Sky Sports News can reveal Newcastle have agreed to pay £9.5m (€11m) compensation to Saudi side Al Ahli for Jaissle.

The German, who previously managed Red Bull Salzburg, will sign a four-year contract at St James' Park.

The plan is for the 38-year-old to meet up with his new players in Spain on Saturday at their training camp in La Manga.

Jaissle's imminent appointment comes after Newcastle officially announced Howe's departure on Friday, a day after Sky Sports News had revealed his exit.

The reason the Howe statement was held up was to allow the club to ensure the Jaissle deal was agreed.

Jaissle's first match in charge will be a pre-season friendly against Valencia at the Mestalla next Saturday.

Howe steps down 'to recharge and take a break'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Redknapp backs former Newcastle head coach Eddie Howe to get back into management at a 'top club'.

Howe says managing Newcastle has been the privilege of his life after confirming he had stepped down as head coach.

The 48-year-old ended the Magpies' 70-year wait for domestic silverware with Carabao Cup glory in 2025, as well as overseeing qualification for the Champions League twice.

The Premier League club confirmed his exit on Friday afternoon, saying they had accepted his decision to step down and thanked him for his "extraordinary contribution".

Departing Howe said in a lengthy statement: "After a period of personal reflection, I have decided that now is the right time for me to step away from my role as head coach of Newcastle United.

"After nearly five years of giving my life, heart and soul into the club with unrelenting energy, I feel that it is in the best interests of both myself and the club to step away, recharge and take a break.

"Although it's been incredibly difficult to make this decision, I know in my heart that it's the right one. I have always put the best interests of Newcastle before my own in every single decision I have made whilst I've been here and this one is no different.

"It has been the privilege of my lifetime to have been the manager of Newcastle United.

"It is difficult to put into words what this club, the city and its supporters mean, and will always mean, to me and my family."

Howe's heartfelt 547-word message reflected on the highs and lows of his time in the north east, where he created memories that he will "cherish for the rest of my life".

Newcastle chief executive David Hopkinson added: "Eddie and his staff leave with the deep gratitude and respect of everyone at Newcastle United, and with a lasting place in the club's history.

"While we are naturally disappointed to see Eddie leave, we remain immensely thankful for everything he has done for the club.

"On behalf of our owners, board, players, staff and supporters, I would like to extend sincere thanks to Eddie for his outstanding service and leadership, and wish him and his family every success and happiness for the future."

Howe is followed out of St James' Park by coaches Jason Tindall, Graeme Jones, Stephen Purches and Simon Weatherstone, as well as head of performance Dan Hodges.

'King of this club!' - Guimaraes posts Howe farewell message

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Redknapp believes Bruno Guimaraes can benefit from Eddie Howe leaving Newcastle

Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes has called Howe the 'king of this club' following the head coach's exit.

Howe's resignation comes amid Arsenal's interest in Guimaraes, who has praised his former boss.

In an Instagram post, Guimaraes wrote the words over a picture of Howe: "King of this club!!

"Thanks for everything you've done for us. I loved enjoying our time together. Thanks for making me a better player and person!

"No words I can say will really say how much I enjoyed being your player. "Wish you all the very best in your future, gaffer."

Hornicek to be first-choice goalkeeper after £25.7m deal agreed

Image: Lukas Hornicek is set to join Newcastle from Braga

Newcastle have an agreement in principle with Braga for Lukas Hornicek, who is being brought in to be the club's first-choice goalkeeper.

Newcastle have agreed to activate his £25.7m (€30m) release clause, and are now discussing payment terms with the Portuguese club.

The 24-year-old Czech has been given permission to travel for a medical, as the two clubs tie up the loose ends of a deal.

He will become their fifth signing of the summer, taking the spending to £140m.

Sports.title: Chelsea's Mudryk cleared to play after doping ban resolved
Sports.content:
Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk has been cleared to return to play after his doping ban was resolved.

The 25-year-old has not played competitively since November 2024 after he was suspended for four years for failing a drug test, which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance, two years ago.

Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) while changes to World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) procedures in the interim mean that had his failed test produced the same result now, charges would not have been brought.

The FA said: "Changes have been made… which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk's sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no anti-doping rule violations would have resulted.

"Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, the FA and Mr Mudryk have now - with the agreement of WADA - resolved the appeal proceedings.

"As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the ADRVs (Anti-Doping Rule Violations) charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement.

"Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect."
