Sports.title: How Glasgow's hometown hero Josh Kerr is relishing his battle for Commonwealth gold after shattering fastest mile world record... and why he wants to be under as much pressure as possible, writes NIK SIMON
Sports.content:
How Glasgow's hometown hero Josh Kerr is relishing his battle for Commonwealth gold after shattering fastest mile world record... and why he wants to be under as much pressure as possible, writes NIK SIMON

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Step off the train at Glasgow Central and one of the first things you see is an enormous billboard of Josh Kerr.

It is a giant image of the hometown hero, letting out a cathartic roar after he shattered the world record for the men's outdoor mile two weeks ago.

Scotland expects their 28-year-old runner to win gold but this weekend’s big-ticket race promises to be the highest quality showdown of these scaled-down Games.

It is the first time the mile has featured for 60 years – having been replaced by the 1,500 metres – and organisers hope it will stir up memories of the historic duel between Roger Bannister and John Landy.

Kerr faces world class opposition. Former world champion Jake Wightman – also of Scotland – defending Commonwealth champion Oliver Hoare and breakthrough star Cameron Myers complete a formidable field.

‘I thrive in a pressure environment,’ said Kerr, who turned his bedroom into an altitude chamber before breaking the record.

Josh Kerr set a new world record for the fastest mile - with a time of 3mins and 42.66secs

Scotland expects their 28-year-old star to win gold at the Commonwealth Games this weekend

‘I want as much pressure on me as possible. I’m here to show up and get a gold medal for Scotland, and hopefully we can put more people on the podium than just me.

‘I think the other Scottish guys are looking great, and Jake’s run an awesome kilometre, so I’m just happy to be rubbing shoulders with these guys again and going after the big medals.’

The conditions at Scotstoun will be a far cry from the perfect settings Kerr enjoyed for his world-record run. There will be no pacemakers and the Scottish weather is unpredictable. It will be a tactical battle of pacing, positioning and the final kick.

‘It is very different to go from racing a clock to racing these guys - these are some of the best milers in the world,’ added Kerr. ‘Just trying to battle against them and try to win at my tactical battle.

‘It's going to be a war out there. It's the home crowd, it’s our track, it's where we learnt, it's our crowd. The rest of the guys want to take what’s ours. They will have to come with something because they are not going to get it easy.’

Kerr trained at Scotstoun as a teenager and also watched his older brother, Jake, play rugby there for Edinburgh against Glasgow Warriors. Fellow Scot Wightman is also familiar with the surroundings and believes the headline event can provide the moment of the Games.

‘I looked down every single start list of the track events and there are so many missing every other event,’ said Wightman. ‘When you look at ours, there’s not one person you probably could have added into this to make it any stronger.

‘The irony is that I think every event you’d say that the European field would be harder than the Commonwealth; whereas ours the Commonwealth is so much harder than the European one. It will bring the whole world’s attention onto it.

‘I think sometimes the Commonwealths get stuck in our bubble of nations that are competing and you speak to Americans sometimes and they haven’t even heard of it; whereas I feel like there’s enough interest in the mile, especially after what Josh did.

It is the first time the mile has featured for 60 years - having been replaced by the 1,500 metres - and the race promises to be the highest quality showdown of these scaled-down Games

‘I think there’s going to be a big audience around the world tuning in for this, which would be cool for the legacy of Commonwealth and for an event that seemed like it might not keep happening just because of the funding and who’s going to pick it up.

'I think if we can put on a good show on Saturday it’s a real good thing for Commonwealth sport in the future. If we can write headlines because it’s an amazing race and there’s something really good to see then maybe it will help keep pushing the Commonwealths to get back to where it should be.’

Sports.title: Andy Burnham calls for Gianni Infantino to RESIGN: Prime Minister tells under-fire FIFA president he is 'the wrong man' to lead football in wake of World Cup backlash
Sports.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has joined the growing contingent calling for FIFA President Gianni Infantino to resign over his plans to introduce private investment into the World Cup.

Burnham, an Everton fan, has said Infantino - who wants to generate £3.1billion in private investment in the World Cup - is no longer fit to govern world football.

It comes after UEFA announced a boycott of FIFA competitions over the plans while Concacaf and the AFC also opposed the proposals.

The AFC went as far to urge FIFA to undertake an urgent review of their leadership.

Speaking to reporters in Sheffield, Burnham said: 'This was an outrageous suggestion.

'The idea that it could even be brought forward shows that, in my view, [he] is the wrong man to lead the organisation.'

Chancellor John Healey added: 'I think FIFA's plans are falling apart, and I'm dead proud that the FA and UEFA have led the charge against the idea that the World Cup is for sale.

'The prime minister is right when he says football is for the fans. I want to see these plans put to one side and let's concentrate on the football.'

Concacaf nations are understood to be losing faith - or have already lost confidence - in the FIFA president.

Andy Burnham has joined the growing calls for FIFA president Gianni Infantino to resign

FIFA have 211 member nations, meaning 106 signatories are required to block or approve any changes to their statutes. 135 nations have voiced opposition to Infantino’s plans - he does not have the votes.

Should Infantino press ahead or abandon the plans but try to remain FIFA’s kingpin, discontented nations could convene an emergency FIFA congress to initiate a vote of no confidence.

Only 20 per cent of FIFA members are required to trigger a vote, meaning support from all of UEFA’s members or CONCACAF’s 46 FIFA-registered nations would be sufficient.

Sources have suggested that Norway have floated an emergency congress while all options remain on the table for UEFA nations.

Burnham is the latest high-profile British politician to oppose Infantino after Reform UK leader Nigel Farage urged the Swiss football administrator to step down on Thursday night. 'Football is for the people,' Farage posted on X. 'UEFA are right to take a stand and Gianni Infantino must resign.'

In support of UEFA's boycott, Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy added: 'This is a principled decision that we strongly support. Football belongs to the fans, not billionaire investors. Enough is enough. It's time to take a stand to protect our game.'

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino's most bitter rival: Meet UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin - the Slovenian lawyer taking on FIFA's plan to sell the World Cup
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino's most bitter rival: Meet UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin - the Slovenian lawyer taking on FIFA's plan to sell the World Cup

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

As football's elite gathered in the hospitality seating at the MetLife Stadium in New York to watch Spain take on Argentina in this month's World Cup final, one FIFA luminary was conspicuous in his absence.

Aleksander Ceferin holds the position of vice president of football's international governing body as well as that of president of UEFA. But rather than watch the tie and see one of his own federations lift the trophy, the Slovenian executive pointedly snubbed the event - reportedly over FIFA's controversial decision to suspend US star Folarin Balogun's red card.

In the wake of Balogun's seemingly Donald Trump-influenced amnesty, UEFA said that FIFA's decision to defer his one-match ban had 'crossed a red line'. Less than a month later, FIFA president Gianni Infantino has sailed over another.

Since the revelation of the leaked proposal to sell £3.1billion-worth of shares in FIFA's tournaments to an investor group led by the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, Infantino has attracted widespread condemnation.

But few voices were as forthright in their disapproval as Ceferin's UEFA, whose European members voted on Thursday to boycott FIFA tournaments in opposition to the proposal, a move since taken up by the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF.

This is not Ceferin's first battle against Infantino's FIFA, however, with the pair increasingly at loggerheads over the direction of international football. The two men have a checkered recent past that has at times seen Ceferin appear actively defiant of FIFA's age of expansion under the scheming Swiss-Italian.

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin is the loudest opponent to the controversial proposal pitched by his opposite number at FIFA, Gianni Infantino

The Swiss-Italian executive is attempting to sell £1.3bn-worth of shares in FIFA's tournaments

Ceferin's background in sports law, which he began practising following his graduation from the University of Ljubljana, eventually saw him step into his first position in sports administration as the head of the Slovenian Football Association.

In a quirk of fate, both Ceferin and Infantino ascended to their current roles in 2016. The duo had previously worked together at UEFA in the early 2010s, when Infantino held the role of Secretary General and Ceferin of second and third vice-chairman of its Legal Committee.

Their mutual history, however, has not appeared to breed a warm and friendly relationship.

UEFA's disapproval of how FIFA had handled Balogun's red card - which they described as an 'unprecedented, incomprehensible and unjustifiable' act - was far from the governing body's only disapproval with this year's World Cup.

As FIFA weathered terrible publicity for their lack of action as Trump's administration barred FIFA-approved referee, the Somalian Omar Artan, from entering the country, UEFA joined the pile-on in style.

Artan, UEFA announced, would be welcomed to officiate their Super Cup final between Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain and Europa League winners Aston Villa in August. The appointment will be the highest-profile of the 34-year-old's career.

As much as the gesture was a sympathetic one of goodwill after Artan was unable to become the first-ever Somali referee at a World Cup, UEFA might have enjoyed the opportunity for some point-scoring over FIFA, who were accused of abandoning their values to roll over for Trump's.

Under Ceferin, UEFA also disagreed with some of FIFA's regulation changes brought in for this year's World Cup, including the use of mandatory 'hydration breaks' to provide more airtime for advertising.

UEFA have confirmed that hydration breaks will not be present at the 2028 European Championships, nor will their referees be sanctioning players who cover their mouth when speaking to their rivals as FIFA did in June and July.

The organisation also staunchly opposed plans to expand the World Cup even more than the 48 teams who played in 2026's overstuffed edition.

In April, Ceferin called the idea of having 64 teams play in the 2030 iteration a 'bad' one and admitted that Infantino's proposal on the matter had been 'maybe even more surprising for me' than for fans.

Ceferin and Infantino have seen their mutual organisations clash over a number of issues in recent years

In a twist of fate, the two men were both elected into their current positions 10 years ago

Relations between the two have been on a knife's edge for some time, with Ceferin thought to have been particularly incensed by Infantino's conduct during FIFA's annual Congress last May.

Infantino arrived more than two hours late for the meeting after accompanying Trump on a diplomatic tour of the Middle East. During a break in proceedings, Ceferin led a walkout of some European FIFA member association representatives and accused Infantino of putting 'private political interests' ahead of football governance.

Naturally, Infantino rebuffed this.

'As president of FIFA my responsibility is to make decisions in the interests of the organization,' Infantino said. 'I felt that I needed to be there to represent football and all of you.'

Ceferin subsequently boycotted this year's Congress.

Significant fractures appeared with FIFA's relaunch of the Club World Cup tournament, expanded and given additional sheen in the form of a bumper £84m payday for eventual winners Chelsea and a Tiffany and Co-designed trophy.

The new-look Club World Cup was viewed as an existential threat to UEFA's own flagship competition, the Champions League, and as early as 2018, Ceferin went on the attack.

Then, the plans were rolled into suggestions of a rolling Nations League tournament with a new mini-World Cup every second October, and Ceferin accused Infantino of 'selling the soul of football' in an early harbinger of this most recent FIFA controversy.

'As long as I am UEFA president there will be no room for pursuing selfish endeavours or hiding behind false pretences,' Ceferin said. 'I cannot accept that some people who are blinded by the pursuit of profit are considering to sell the soul of football tournaments to nebulous private funds.

'Money does not rule - and the European sports model must be respected. Football is not for sale. I will not let anyone sacrifice its structures on the altar of a highly cynical and ruthless mercantilism.'

When the Club World Cup did eventually come to pass, elongating an already stuffed 2024-25 season, Ceferin was more sanguine, but warned of the dangers of overplaying stars.

'The calendar is oversaturated,' he says. 'So much so that we can no longer add new matches. And I agree with that.

'But the situation is paradoxical. On one side, clubs strive for financial sustainability and need more games to generate profit. On the other side, players are overloaded and getting injured.'

But Ceferin's crusades have not begun and ended with FIFA.

In 2021, Ceferin led the charge against the bombshell breakaway European Super League (ESL), which saw nine top clubs including Barcelona, Real Madrid and Manchester United announce their plans for a new tournament on the eve of a UEFA Executive Committee meeting to discuss revamping the Champions League.

Since becoming UEFA president, Ceferin has attempted to thwart a number of new innovations

Juventus chairman Andrea Agnelli's role in the breakaway European Super League was personally troubling for him, due to their close friendship

While universally reviled by fans for its inherent lack of competitiveness and closed-shop 'permanent member' format, Ceferin was a particularly vocal opponent. Not least because he had been personally deceived by founders including Juventus chairman Andrea Agnelli - whose daughter he counts as one of his godchildren.

Ceferin immediately sought to ban the clubs from their competitions as the two sides waged legal war against one another, with a UEFA statement calling the new tournament 'a spit in the face of football lovers and of society as a whole'.

'Our game has become the greatest sport in the world based on open competition, integrity and sporting merit,' The firebrand statement continued, hours after the announcement. 'We cannot and will not allow that to change. Never, ever.

'We urge everyone from the millions of football lovers around the world, the world's media, politicians and football's governing bodies to stand tall with us, as we do everything in our power to ensure this never ends up in fruition.'

So determined was Ceferin to bar the league from getting off the ground that he suggested that players at the clubs involved would be banned from competing for their relevant countries at the upcoming Euro 2020.

But knowing when to play nice, the Slovenian welcomed those clubs who promptly withdrew against the backdrop of fan protest in the streets with open arms.

Ceferin later compared the experience to his time in the army, when he was called up to fight in the Slovenian Territorial Army during their war of independence as Yugoslavia collapsed in 1991.

'It finished very soon, in 10 days, but there was a lot of tension - day and night - and threats and bombs,' Ceferin told AP of the war in an interview shortly after crushing the ESL. 'It's an experience that helps you to survive if some people then try to destabilize you.'

'Psychologically, (the announcement) was such a shock for me. Similar to the war. You cannot compare, but both were stressful - the tension was similar.'

But, he added: 'Spoiled children cannot destabilise me.'

Ceferin may be keen to posit himself as an avenging angel in the face of forces determined to sell football to the highest bidder, but his own background is not entirely stainless.

An investigation by independent outlet Josimar in 2017 alleged that he had lacked the credentials necessary for his appointment as head of the Slovenian FA, as he did not have the mandatory minimum five years of football boardroom experience. In that election, he ran unopposed, after his would-be rival Tugo Frajman withdrew and offered Ceferin's 'dirty campaigning' as his reason for doing so.

In the lengths Infantino has gone to conceal his controversial proposal and attempt to force FIFA's member associations to fall in line, the president has shown he has no interest in playing by the rules. Perhaps the fact that his most bitter rival is no angel could mean that Infantino has met his match.

Sports.title: 'Some people prefer Manchester or London... but I love Burnley': How $100m NFL star JJ Watt has embraced his role as Clarets co-owner - and even designed their new shirt
Sports.content:
JJ Watt wants to restore the Burnley of old. For a man used to the glitzy environs of America's NFL, who once had a $100million contract and lived in a place called Paradise Valley, he comes across remarkably in touch with this humble corner of Lancashire which he claims to love.

'For a very long time, you knew what you were getting at Burnley,' the club's minority owner tells Daily Mail Sport. 'You were in for a fight.

'I want a strong identity. We are going to outwork everybody, we are going to out-tough everybody. You are in for a very long day.'

If this all sounds rather Sean Dyche-coded, you'd be right. Burnley lacked their usual grit last season. The Clarets are back in the Championship after an abysmal relegation – their fifth divisional change in as many seasons. They won one of their last 29 games and had the league's worst defensive record. Pride in the shirt feels at a low ebb and, as such, Watt has made a change.

Burnley have released a new away kit, designed by Watt over the course of two years, which harks back to the club's history and resurrects an old crest. He spent time filming the promo on a nearby dairy farm and driving a milk cart over Lancastrian potholes. For a man who repeats the word 'work' 10 times during our interview, it feels fitting.

'The history and tradition of the club is what makes it special,' says Watt. 'Maybe some people prefer London or Manchester, but going around Burnley, I love it.

Burnley co-owner JJ Watt is hoping they can fight their way out of the Championship again

The Clarets are aiming to be promoted from the second tier for a third consecutive time

'We’re trying to really capture the essence of what Burnley is. The reason I built this kit is to try and preserve that history.'

It will take more than a polyester jersey and sweet talk to dispel the gloom from Turf Moor. They last won at home 286 days ago, when England had only just qualified for the World Cup.

First-team stars in Jaidon Anthony and Maxime Esteve have left, while Lesley Ugochukwu has gone on loan to Galatasaray. Scott Parker was sacked in April and the Clarets have appointed Nicky Hayen, who won the Belgian Pro League with Club Brugge in 2023-24, as his successor. It is a gamble.

'One of the first things Nicky said when he came in was that we need to train twice a day,' says Watt, a former Pizza Hut delivery man. 'I absolutely love that. It’s all about his work ethic, his tactics, his aggressiveness. We always want to be on the front foot.

'He wants these guys to have no egos, to put the crest before their last name, and it’s been great so far.'

'Great' is perhaps a stretch – Burnley are winless in five pre-season games against Cincinnati, Columbus Crew, Real Salt Lake, Ajax, and sister club Espanyol, though Hayen took a watching brief for the first two.

Watt wants to add his expertise without being overbearing. He and Hayen will discuss tactics, set-pieces and how to optimise a player's diet and recovery.

They have already gone about reinforcing the midfield, making Florentino's loan from Benfica permanent for £20.8million, and bringing in Ugo Raghouber from Lille.

The former NFL star models their new away kit, which harkens back to the club's history

He relies on the support of his wife Kealia, a former United States international player

Former Club Brugge manager Nicky Hayen - who won them a league title - has taken the reins

Watt has been involved with Burnley for three years and his arrival was treated with some scepticism. When 12 of the Premier League's 20 clubs have American owners, the last thing many traditional English fans want is another new face from across the pond with their bombast and unusual sporting ideas – though some years, Burnley fans probably wouldn't mind scrapping relegation.

To his credit, Watt is a long-time follower of football and speaks with authenticity. He played as a kid, watched matches at the crack of dawn as an NFL player, and his wife, Kealia, is a former United States international. Crucially, during our chat at least, he calls the sport by its correct name.

'I was drawn to the English game because of the passion, the history, and traditions,' he says.

'My favourite custom by far is my matchday routine where I get dropped off at the Royal Dyche and have a pint of Guinness with everybody there.

'Then I take a little walk around the corner to Burnley Miners' Club where I get myself one Bene Bomb. Then I walk the rest of the way into the Bob Lord Stand and get myself ready for the match. I meet supporters and hear the pulse of what they’re thinking.'

He can't always be in England for matches, but watches from Houston. Burnley are gathering popularity Stateside, where they spent some of pre-season.

‘It’s pretty funny how matchday has grown. My phone used to be silent on matchdays when we won or scored,' he explains.

'I’d text somebody and say, “hey, we just won,” and they’d say, “I didn’t know it was on.” Now, my phone is blowing up the second we score. My dad is texting me, I’ve got random people coming out of the woodwork. I’ll know if my TV is lagging or not because I’ll have everybody texting me when I haven’t seen a goal yet.

'It’s been really cool to see so many Burnley fans, random kids on the streets wearing old Burnley kits.’

Whether they'll come to treasure the new away strip will depend partly on the memories they make in it. Promotion is the target. As ever, the Championship remains an unpredictable beast.

Sports.title: Paddy Power predict under-fire Gianni Infantino WILL remain as FIFA president at the end of the year - despite huge backlash over controversial World Cup scheme
Sports.content:
Paddy Power believe Gianni Infantino will still be FIFA president by the end of the year - despite widespread condemnation of his plans to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino, 56, is facing a rebellion from his members and is under pressure to quit but is odds-on at 1/4 with Paddy Power to keep his job, with the next election scheduled for March 2027.

The controversial Swiss-Italian is 3/1 not to be at the helm of FIFA on December 31.

The bookmaker earlier brutally put the boot in on FIFA and Infantino over the governing body's jaw-dropping private investment plans for the World Cup.

The fallout and controversy from the leaked proposal about FIFA's desire to generate £3.1billion in private investment by selling off a portion of the tournament, along with the Club World Cup, has been significant.

UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC have all come out against Infantino's plot, while one of his most senior advisors Carlos Cordeiro also resigned in protest.

Paddy Power put a mysterious green 'FOR SALE' sign outside FIFA HQ in Switzerland

And now Paddy Power have had their say, with the bookmaker aiming a hilarious dig at the governing body.

In response to the plan and FIFA's alleged desperation to bring in outside investment, a mysterious green 'FOR SALE' sign was spotted outside FIFA HQ in Zurich, Switzerland.

A message on the sign read: 'To anyone – anyone – with money, power and a willingness to endure Gianni’s small talk.'

The stunt was revealed on social media on Friday morning, with a man dressed in a green cap seen hammering the sign into the ground.

A Paddy Power spokesperson said: 'Astronomical ticket prices. Inflated hotel room rates. A diabolical half-time show.

'Just when you think you’ve seen it all from Gianni Infantino, he goes and puts the World Cup on the market.

'We thought that might be one thing that isn’t up for grabs, but Gianni seems to think otherwise, so we’ve lent him a sign to tell suitors football is officially for sale.'

With the opposition from UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC - plus Infantino's own inner circle - the proposal now appears to be dead in the water.

This is because 135 FIFA members are now publicly opposed to the FIFA Forward Enterprise - the name of the new company Infantino wants to set up to run the tournaments - bringing the dissidents above the required 106 threshold to block the plan.

When announcing his resignation, Cordeiro distanced himself from Infantino’s plot and ripped into the proposal.

He also called on his now former FIFA colleagues to follow suit and speak out against the plan, which he describes as a bad deal for football. Infantino had promised member associations a £30million incentive to force the deal through.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham joined the growing calls for Infantino to resign from his role on Friday afternoon.

Sports.title: Arsene Wenger has ruined his own legacy. We once thought he was The Professor, now we see the truth - a silent stooge following his master Gianni Infantino... and is ex-Arsenal boss the real brains behind FIFA's hated schemes?
Sports.content:
Speaking in February on the tenth anniversary of Gianni Infantino’s accession as FIFA president, Arsene Wenger paid tribute to his friend for overseeing a ‘huge improvement’ in world football.

‘Gianni is always ready to move forward and to create new ideas. He’s open to new ideas,’ said Wenger.

Say what you want about Infantino, he’s most definitely open to ideas.

The idea to have a World Cup in Qatar at Christmas time, and increase the number of teams at the tournament this summer to 48. If he gets his way, it will be 64 in four years’ time, when the tournament is already being played across six countries.

The idea to introduce mandatory hydration breaks at the World Cup this summer, thinking we wouldn’t see them for the commercial grab they really were, and to have the finalists from Spain and Argentina kicking their heels in the dressing room at half-time for the best part of half an hour waiting for Madonna and Co to get off the pitch at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

It was Infantino’s idea to award President Donald Trump the ridiculous FIFA Peace Prize, and then say nothing when the Iran team were banished to train in Mexico while Trump's war against them raged in the Middle East, or when the Somalian referee Omar Artan was denied entry to the US.

‘Gianni Infantino is always ready to move forward and to create new ideas. He’s open to new ideas,’ said Arsene Wenger

Say what you want about Infantino, he’s most definitely open to ideas

And it’s his preposterous idea to carve up the World Cup and sell it to private investors for £3.1billion by strong-arming FIFA’s 211 member associations into accepting his proposals, thus plunging world football into crisis.

All the while, Wenger has hovered at Infantino’s right hand like a silent stooge, a sight we witnessed so often in North America this summer.

As FIFA’s chief of global football development, the 76-year-old Frenchman is part of Infantino’s inner circle. One of the people, it’s fair to assume, who would have been aware of the great World Cup sell-off when so many other executives weren’t. For all we know, Wenger may have played an active role in hatching the plot given that he has Infantino’s ear.

Either way, it’s not a good look for the man English football first came to know 30 years ago when he arrived from Japan to take over as Arsenal manager.

The Professor, they called him. The forward-thinking coach whose ideas had a profound effect on the Arsenal culture and beyond the marbled halls of Highbury.

Wenger has continued to influence football’s development since he was appointed by Infantino in November 2019, 18 months after he had left Arsenal after 22 years in charge.

Among other things, he heads up the £160million FIFA Talent Coach Programme which develops young players in poorer countries where the path to professional football is lacking, and for that he deserves credit. He also leads a FIFA taskforce on player welfare which aims to address concerns over the increasing demands of the football calendar, although how Wenger’s proposal to stage the World Cup every two years would help in that regard is anyone’s guess.

It would be refreshing to think that a man of his influence and intelligence would be able to stand up to Infantino’s rampant egotism, but sadly that doesn’t seem to be the case.

It’s not a good look for the man English football first came to know 30 years ago when he arrived from Japan to take over as Arsenal manager and turned them into champions

Wenger will do what he always does these days. He will follow his master and nod along to whatever hare-brained idea Infantino comes up with next

Before the World Cup final, he claimed the new 48-team format had been a success – though at least had the decency to admit that not everyone was a fan of the hydration breaks.

It would be fascinating to hear what Wenger really thinks of the plan to sell off the World Cup and Infantino’s offer to give member associations £30million if they accept it by September 19, which has met with such resistance around the globe including the threat of a UEFA boycott. But let’s not hold our breath. He will do what he always does these days. He will follow his master and nod along to whatever hare-brained idea Infantino comes up with next.

FIFA tried to extinguish the fire on Friday as its president faced growing calls to step down. ‘Nobody is selling football. This is not something FIFA would ever entertain,’ read a statement.

But they aren’t fooling anyone. The world can see Infantino for what he is now – and we see Wenger standing squarely behind him.

Sports.title: Arsenal reach £77m agreement in principle to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle - as Premier League champions plan medical next week
Sports.content:
Arsenal reach £77m agreement in principle to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle - as Premier League champions plan medical next week

Arsenal have reached an agreement in principle to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle - and have set aside a day next week for the Brazil midfielder's medical.

It is understood that the fee agreed for the Newcastle captain is £77million plus add-ons.

The 28-year-old's contract has not yet been signed and finer details are to be sorted but Daily Mail Sport can confirm a deal is now very close.

The Magpies had been reluctant to part with their captain after losing other key players - such as Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon - this summer but the Premier League champions have gone all out to get the deal done.

Bruno Guimaraes is set to become the latest key Newcastle player to leave this summer

The Brazilian was part of the Newcastle side that won the club's first major trophy for 70 years - the Carabao Cup in March 2025

He is the third key player to leave Newcastle this summer, joining Anthony Gordon (second left) and Sandro Tonali (second right), while manager Eddie Howe has also left the club

As revealed by Daily Mail Sport, Guimaraes dropped a bombshell on the Newcastle hierarchy several weeks ago by informing them of his desire to leave. And he did not fly with the rest of the Toon squad to their pre-season training camp in La Manga on Friday.

The Magpies also saw manager Eddie Howe leave the club yesterday after four and a half years.

He would become Arsenal's fourth signing of the summer, after they made Piero Hincapie's loan deal from Bayer Leverkusen permanent, signed free agent former Leeds United goalkeeper Illan Meslier and struck a £36m deal for Club Brugge's Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

Arsenal first tried to sign Guimaraes in 2022 from Lyon, but Newcastle stole a march on the midfielder, who has won 48 caps for his country and played in this summer's World Cup.

Sports.title: Tennis latest: US Open hit by withdrawal as Carlos Alcaraz stuns fans
Sports.content:
Tennis latest: US Open hit by withdrawal as Carlos Alcaraz stuns fans

The latest tennis headlines ahead of the last major of the season

View 3 Images Carlos Alcaraz has shocked his social media following (Image: Pablo Cuadra/Getty Images for Laureus)

An Australian tennis star who once beat the iconic Serena Williams has withdrawn from the US Open. Meanwhile, Carlos Alcaraz has left fans gobsmacked with a new look ahead of his impending return.

‌



The Spaniard has been sidelined for most of the 2026 season due to a recurring wrist injury. However, fans are building excitement for Alcaraz's return to Flushing Meadows as he shares recovery snaps on Instagram.

‌



Meanwhile, one star who won't be heading Stateside is Ajla Tomljanovic, who bid farewell to a "tough" campaign marred by minor injuries. The Australian announced her withdrawal from the US Open on social media and insists her focus is on the upcoming 2027 season.

‌



Here, Mirror Sport has all the latest tennis news.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Andrew Castle confirms immediate Wimbledon return after emotional BBC exit READ MORE :

Carlos Alcaraz stuns fans

Alcaraz is no stranger to reinventing his hairstyle, but his striking cornrow look has left supporters completely speechless. The Spaniard has experimented with a host of bold styles, having shaved his head at last year's US Open and drawing comparisons to a young David Beckham in the process.

‌



The 23-year-old went platinum blonde with cropped hair before the Laver Cup, before allowing it to grow back to his natural brunette shade ahead of the 2026 season. Following his Australian Open triumph and a string of injury-enforced withdrawals, Alcaraz reverted to a longer, more relaxed style.

This was the very same hairstyle he sported at the World Cup final, where he cheered on his beloved Spain as they defeated Argentina to lift the trophy. Now, eagle-eyed fans have clocked the tennis ace showcasing cornrows in a recent Instagram post.

View 3 Images Carlos Alcaraz is enjoying some new hairstyles (Image: Instagram)

‌



This snapshot was one of 16 images featured in the 'Insta dump' but supporters were most taken aback by this photograph. One branded the look the "unexpected hairstyle of the summer."

Another commented: "For 2 hot seconds... I thought I was looking at a young Drake, sorry Carlos, but glad you're enjoying the summer."

A third noted: "From Blondecaraz to Cornrowlitos, he keeps tennis stylish & fun!" Supporters also mentioned his eagerly-awaited return to tennis while praising his fresh appearance. One stated: "Can't wait to see you and the braids back on court."

‌



Meanwhile, another observed: "The hair we need you to take to the US Open!!"

Tomljanovic withdraws

View 3 Images Ajla Tomljanovic will not compete at Flushing Meadows (Image: Cameron Smith/Getty Images for LTA)

Tomljanovic has withdrawn from the US Open due to minor injuries that have coincided with a 'tough' season. The 33-year-old confirmed on social media that she won't be competing at Flushing Meadows next month and is focused on preparing for next year.

‌



Posting on Instagram, the Australian said: " It has been a tough year battling minor injuries, so I've decided to end my season earlier than planned to be healthy and ready for 2027."

Following her withdrawal, German tennis player Ella Seidel has been entered into the main draw. Tomljanovic's major tennis highlight came at the 2022 US Open, where she knocked Serena Williams out in the third round.

This proved to be Williams' last match ahead of her initial retirement, and the Australian paid tribute to her following the win. She said: "I'm feeling really sorry, just because I love Serena just as much as you guys do. And what she's done for me, for the sport of tennis, is incredible... she is the greatest of all time."

Sports.title: Glorious Goodwood tips: Saturday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy
Sports.content:
Glorious Goodwood tips: Saturday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy

The Coral Stewards Cup is the highlight of the final day of Glorious Goodwood and Newsboy has provided detailed analysis of that and all the other races on Saturday

View 7 Images Newsboy provides tips for Goodwood (Image: PA)

1.50 Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap: VALEDICTORY has the going-places profile, not to mention the local knowledge, to bid his rivals ‘adieu’.

‌



The gelded son of Cracksman, trained in tandem by John and Thady Gosden, has taken his form to a new level since stepping up to a mile and three quarters and being equipped with cheekpieces.

‌



The combination worked a treat when Valedictory beat six opponents over course and distance at the end of May with a length-and-a-half beating of Spinning Wheel. And William Buick’s partner defied a 5lb rise in the weights at Newmarket’s July Festival 22 days ago, getting the better of Roaring Legend by a neck.

‌



Danny Mullins fined £2,500 for conduct near crowd on fractious Willie Mullins horse READ MORE :

Rising star jockey makes history by completing huge Galway Festival double READ MORE :

The latest intervention from the British Horseracing Authority number cruncher means Valedictory, with another 3lb on his back, competes from a mark of 95 today.

But the four-year-old is only just finding his feet and, with more to come, Valedictory has strong claims on the hat-trick. Align The Stars landed this race two years ago and the Northumberland Plate hero has to be respected, along with the Joseph O’Brien pair Aeronautic and Small Fry .

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 VALEDICTORY, 2 ALIGN THE STARS, 3 AERONAUTIC

‌



View 7 Images Al Aasy: fancied by Newsboy (Image: PA)

2.25 Coral Glorious Stakes: AL AASY is evergreen - and ripe for the Glorious Stakes hat-trick. At nine years of age, William Haggas’s stable stalwart is well into the veteran stage of his career but continues to be more than a match for younger legs.

His 12 victories from 30 outings - that’s an impressive 40% strike-rate - include eight triumphs in Group 3 company.

‌



In 2024, Al Aasy beat Relentless Voyager for this prize and he returned 12 months ago to defend his title with a three-length humbling of Meydan.

That effort was all the more meritorious when one considers he carried a 3lb penalty for his success in the same-level Gordon Richards Stakes at Sandown Park in the spring.

There is no such encumbrance today and a return to winning form in Beverley’s Listed Charlie Wood Stakes at the beginning of the month will set Tom Marquand’s mount up perfectly for today

‌



The biggest danger may come from fellow Somerville Lodge trainee Opportunity, with In My Teens and Enfjaar taken to fight it out for the bronze.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 AL AASY, 2 OPPORTUNITY, 3 IN MY TEENS

View 7 Images Willam Haggas: trains Santorini Star (Image: Photo by Alan Crowhurst/Getty Images)

‌



3.00 Qatar Lillie Langtry Stakes: SANTORINI STAR merits the chance to bounce back from a no-show at Royal Ascot last month.

Her challenge for the Group 2 Hardwicke Stakes on the final day of the fixture went badly awry as the William Haggas-saddled mare, a 16-1 chance, came home last of 12 behind Giavellotto.

But forgive that effort - Santorini Star was stepping back to a mile and a half and wearing cheekpieces that are dispensed with today - and the five-year-old daughter of Golden Horn is a definite player here.

‌



Having beaten Consent for the Group 2 Park Hill Fillies’ Stakes at Doncaster in September - the runner-up reversed the form in the top-level Prix de Royallieu at Longchamp next time - Santorini Star made a winning comeback under Tom Marquand against male opposition in the Group 2 Jockey Club Stakes at Newmarket in May.

And she ran another cracker when beaten a short neck by Caballo De Mar for the Group 1 Prix Vicomtesse Vigier over two miles at Longchamp 20 days later, before her Ascot flop.

Santorini Star, a course winner from her only previous visit to Goodwood, will be more at home back up in distance and shouldn’t be written off. Waardah and Danielle finished first and second 12 in this months ago, and should be in the firing line once more.

‌



View 7 Images Sondad: Newsboy's pick (Image: Niall Carson/PA Wire)

3.35 Coral Stewards' Cup: SONDAD has landed two big sprint-handicap pots this season, and a third could be on the way.

The fitting of a visor saw the Washington DC-sired gelding take one step forward after another for the father-and-son training combination of Mick and David Easterby in 2025.

‌



Having scored at Ascot in May of last year, Sondad followed up in a six-furlong event on Derby day at Epsom, finishing his campaign with podium efforts in competitive sprints won by Candy at Ayr (Ayr Silver Cup) and Aramram at Ascot.

And the five-year-old has continued his upward curve this term, stepping forward from a down-the-field effort behind Dark Thirty at York in May to retain his crown at Epsom the following month.

The draw gods didn’t play ball in the Wokingham Handicap at Royal Ascot a fortnight later - his berth in stall two could hardly have been worse - and, in the circumstance, a ninth behind Double Rush rates a commendable effort.

‌



But there were no such issues in another big-money affair on the Irish Oaks undercard at the Curragh last time, when Sondad and Easterby snr’s grand-daughter Jo Mason accounted for old rival Dark Thirty by half a length. He’s 1lb well in under a 6lb penalty and a draw in stall 21 should put Sondad in the thick of the action.

In a typically fiendish Stewards’ Cup, Far Above Dream, Annaf, Stratusnine and 2024 victor Get It are just four horses capable of getting involved.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 SONDAD, 2 FAR ABOVE DREAM, 3 GET IT

‌



View 7 Images Karl Burke: trains Newsboy's tip (Image: PA)

4.10 Phase Eight Handicap: NAVAL LIGHT and 3lb claimer Jack Nicholls are expected to prove a potent combination for the third time in a row.

The winner’s enclosure proved elusive for Havana Grey’s son on his first six visits to the racecourse. But, on the back of a sixth to Ten Carat Harry in a six-furlong handicap at Newmarket on 2,000 Guineas day, Naval Light, ridden by Nicholls for the first time, enjoyed a red-letter day when justifying odds of 2-5 in a maiden over the same trip at Pontefract 20 days later.

‌



Karl Burke then returned the gelded three-year-old to handicap company as Naval Light and Nicholls took on three rivals over seven furlongs at Catterick Bridge.

Sent off at 7-2, my selection swept through from the back of the field to lead inside the final furlong and account for Woodstock by a length and three-quarters.

Hot favourite Haaderr disappointed that day and more is need after a 5lb rise in the weights. But it will be a surprise if Naval Light can’t summon up another personal best and he’s fancied to go in again.

‌



We’re Goosers found the draw, and possibly the one-mile distance, against him in the Britannia Handicap at Royal Ascot and he heads the list of dangers, which also includes Ghost Mode and Ironwill.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 NAVAL LIGHT, 2 WE’RE GOOSERS, 3 IRONWILL

View 7 Images James Doyle: rides Newsboy's tip (Image: PA)

‌



4.45 British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes: MARKET LEADER did enough on his debut at Windsor, despite a defeat at odds-on, to be of interest here.

Punters were falling over themselves to back the 450,000-Euro breeze-up purchase when he took on eight opponents for a six-furlong novice stakes at Windsor 19 days ago - Market Leader went off the 4-5 hotpot.

But they were soon biting their nails when James Doyle’s partner made a sluggish exit from the starting stalls and trailed the field during the early exchanges.

‌



Market Leader then appeared nonplussed when his jockey urged him forwards inside the final quarter mile but did learn on the job in coming home in third, four lengths behind winner Real Bullet.

Given his obvious lack of streetwisdom, Market Leader, who holds an entry in the Group 1 Vincent O’Brien National Stakes at the Curragh next month, looks capable of a big step forward, and the seventh furlong should help.Regency Royal, Speakers Corner and Leadlight all performed with promise first time up and should improve

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 MARKET LEADER, 2 REGENCY ROYAL, 3 SPEAKERS CORNER

‌



View 7 Images Clive Cox trains Newsboy pick (Image: PA)

5.20 Coral Rewards Shaker Handicap: BLUE COURVOISIER, another horse who missed out on the luck of the draw at Royal Ascot, makes plenty of appeal under Saffie Osborne.

The debut winner of a Leicester novice stakes on his first of two outings as a two-year-old in 2025, the son of Sea The Stars made the frame in handicaps at Newmarket and Ascot when returning in the spring.

‌



With Osborne on board for the first time, Blue Courvoisier gave his trainer Clive Cox a third Silver Bowl triumph when holding Langstone by a length and a half at Carlisle - the one-mile handicap was switched from Haydock Park - at the end of May.

Blue Courvoisier couldn’t get involved from stall one when 18th of 30 in the Britannia Handicap but shouldn’t be written off.

In a wide-open meeting finale, Crest Of Fire, El Matador, Boyfriend and Great Chieftain are names to throw into the mix.

Sports.title: Real Madrid make final Vinicius Jr decision as Arsenal put on transfer red alert
Sports.content:
Real Madrid make final Vinicius Jr decision as Arsenal put on transfer red alert

Vinicius Jr has just one year left on his deal at Real Madrid and Arsenal hope to tempt the forward to join them at the Emirates Stadium this summer

View 2 Images Vinicius Junior is a transfer target for Arsenal (Image: (Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images))

Real Madrid have tabled a final take it or leave it contract offer to Vinicius Junior as he continues to attract interest from Arsenal. The Gunners have enquired about the Brazil international, as boss Mikel Arteta wants to sign proven talent this summer.

‌



Vinicius fits the bill, winning 14 trophies and scoring 128 goals in 375 matches for the Spanish giants, but he only has one year remaining on his current deal. Real have tried to renew Vinicius' deal and opened further talks with him earlier this week, but with no progress made, they have now hit their star man with an ultimatum.

‌



According to Spanish publication Marca, the La Liga giants have informed the 26-year-old’s camp that the latest contract offer they submitted is final and there will be no further increase nor another round of negotiations. If Vinicius accepts, his deal will be renewed, however, if he rejects the offer Real will open the door to a sale this summer to prevent the Brazilian from entering his final year of contract year and leaving for free later, according to Marca.

‌



The Gunners have already bolstered their attacking options this summer with the £34million signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge earlier this month. Arteta admitted he will 'require a better squad and better individuals' for the forthcoming season in an interview with the club’s inhouse media channels earlier this week.

He said: “This has to be the start and this has to be the standard. Excellence has to be our standard and this has to drive us to attack the future.

“The way we behave daily with more and more determination and ambition because we’ve shown that we’ve got it. Now we have to show that we belong to this level and we want to increase and take this football club to a different dimension.”

He added: “We all know about the context of this transfer window. From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level.

“That is going to require a better squad, better individuals. We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way.”

‌



View 2 Images Mikel Arteta wants to sign Vinicius Jr (Image: Getty )

While Josh Kroenke declared Arsenal won’t be standing still this summer after watching his side lift the Premier League title last season. Speaking to NBC, he said: “The business never stops. Right now there are already other teams who are trying to strengthen and come at us for next season.

“We need to be aware of that. We’ve already had a few different conversations about different areas where we think we can improve on and off the pitch.

“I am looking forward to getting that going this summer but it’s going to be an interesting one because of the World Cup but fortunately everyone is coming to the United States so I don’t have to travel.”

Sports.title: Matthias Jaissle can hand Newcastle chance to sign title winner and help fill Anthony Gordon void
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle can hand Newcastle chance to sign title winner and help fill Anthony Gordon void

Newcastle United look to be closing in on appointing Matthias Jaissle as the replacement for Eddie Howe.

View 2 Images Newcastle United look set to appoint Matthias Jaissle as their new head coach. (Image: Yasser Bakhsh/Getty Images))

It’s set to be all change for Newcastle United this summer, both in the dugout and on the pitch. After five years in charge of the club, Eddie Howe has left St James’ Park.

‌



The news broke just a matter of hours after the 4-1 friendly defeat against Championship side Bristol City. It seems to be a time of Chaos for Newcastle.

‌



The manager is said to have made the decision, which follows the sales of Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon earlier this summer. Gordon moved to Barcelona for a fee of £69.3 million, with Tonali completing a £100 million transfer to Tottenham.

‌



The Premier League special edition is on sale now READ MORE :

Bruno Guimaraes pushes for Arsenal transfer with Newcastle agreement imminent READ MORE :

There is also speculation over the futures of both Bruno Guimaraes and Lewis Hall. Arsenal are being strongly linked with Guimaraes , and Manchester United interested in Hall.

For Newcastle, the focus will be on bringing in replacements for Howe and handling any outgoings between now and the Premier League opener. The Magpies seem to be closing in on a deal for Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle.

If that appointment is made, then it could potentially open up the door for Newcastle to move for a former Premier League title winner, who could help to fill some of the void of the quality left by the sales.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

While at Al-Ahil, Jaissle has worked closely with Riyad Mahrez. Under the German coach, he played 122 games, scoring 37 times and providing 50 assists.

The 35-year-old officially left the club this summer and is now available on a free transfer. He could be a player who Jaissle could turn to as he looks to make an impact at Newcastle.

‌



Mahrez’s age and the fact that he has been playing in Saudi Arabia means that he may not be expected to start every game. Newcastle have already brought in a replacement for Gordon in Bazoumana Toure.

View 2 Images Riyad Mahrez is available on a free transfer this summer. (Image: Ercin Erturk/Anadolu via Getty Images)

But, Mahrez, who has won five Premier League titles with Leicester City and Manchester City, would no doubt add some Premier League know-how and quality to Newcastle’s squad.

‌



Speaking about his relationship with Mahrez in December 2024, Jaissle told RMC Sport: "Mahrez is a fantastic footballer, I have a very good relationship with him. And I think if you ask him, he'll probably tell you the same thing.

“I can only say that I'm really happy to have him on the team. He's an incredible player, he's won everything. And he's showing it again this year with the difference he's able to make during matches.”

Mahrez captained Algeria in this summer’s World Cup, scoring twice and providing an assist in his four appearances in the competition. He announced his retirement from international football following the tournament, meaning he’ll be concentrating on his club career.

Article continues below

Fabrizio Romano reports that he is keen to return to Europe, with Serie A Clubs showing an interest. Despite his age, having the chance to sign someone of Mahrez’s quality may be one that Newcastle shouldn’t turn down.

Sports.title: Newcastle United confirm Eddie Howe exit with statement issued as replacement lined up
Sports.content:
Newcastle United confirm Eddie Howe exit with statement issued as replacement lined up

Eddie Howe ended Newcastle United's barren run without a major trophy but will now depart the club after nearly five years of service

View 2 Images Eddie Howe has walked away from his role as Newcastle United boss (Image: MI News/NurPhoto)

Newcastle United have confirmed Eddie Howe has resigned from his position as manager. Earlier reports had stated the Englishman was set to walk away from the club after nearly five years at the helm.

‌



He was the first permanent manager to be appointed by the club after the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund's takeover toward the end of 2021. The ex-Bournemouth manager guided the Magpies into the Champions League on two occasions and won the League Cup to end their 70-year wait without a trophy.

‌



However, things grew more difficult for Howe when Alexander Isak joined Liverpool for £125million and while around £240m was spent on new signings, the club struggled to a 12th placed Premier League finish. After seeing Anthony Gordon join Barcelona, Sandro Tonali join Tottenham Hotspur for £100m and Bruno Guimaraes inform the club he also wants to depart, Howe's resignation has been confirmed.

‌



Newcastle confirmed the news in a statement, which read: "Newcastle United can announce that Eddie Howe has informed the club of his decision to step down as head coach.

Bruno Guimaraes pushes for Arsenal transfer with Newcastle agreement imminent READ MORE :

Bruno Guimaraes given separate Newcastle plan as showdown transfer talks scheduled READ MORE :

"The club has accepted Eddie’s decision and would like to thank him for his extraordinary contribution.

"Also leaving the club are coaches Jason Tindall, Graeme Jones, Stephen Purches and Simon Weatherstone, and head of performance Dan Hodges."

‌



Howe went on to issue an emotional farewell message to Newcastle fans, with the 48-year-old saying: “After a period of personal reflection, I have decided that now is the right time for me to step away from my role as head coach of Newcastle United.

“After nearly five years of giving my life, heart and soul into the club with unrelenting energy, I feel that it is in the best interests of both myself and the club to step away, recharge and take a break.

“Although it’s been incredibly difficult to make this decision, I know in my heart that it’s the right one. I have always put the best interests of Newcastle before my own in every single decision I have made whilst I’ve been here and this one is no different.

‌



“It has been the privilege of my lifetime to have been the manager of Newcastle United.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

“It is difficult to put into words what this club, the city and its supporters mean, and will always mean, to me and my family. From the moment myself, Jason and all of the staff arrived nearly half a decade ago, Newcastle instantly felt like home and the people here welcomed us with open arms. We took huge pride in representing the club from day one and this city will always hold a very special place in our hearts.

‌



“There have been so many incredible moments in our time here. From fighting relegation in our first season to the numerous unforgettable nights at St. James’ Park in the Champions League soon after. The progression was fast.

“Everyone came together, united and what a force we became, culminating in bringing home our first domestic trophy in 70 years. These are all memories that I will cherish for the rest of my life.

“I would like to put on record my sincere thanks and appreciation to Yasir Al-Rumayyan, Jamie Reuben, Jacobo Solís and everyone at PIF, David Hopkinson, Ross Wilson and the entire ownership and leadership group for placing their trust in me and for giving me the opportunity to lead this special football club.

‌



“I remain incredibly positive and enthusiastic about the future of Newcastle. The club is in fantastic hands with a great leadership team and I have no doubt together, alongside whoever comes in to replace me, they will continue to deliver success on the pitch.

View 2 Images Eddie Howe has officially left Newcastle United (Image: David Davies/PA Wire)

“Thank you to Jason Tindall, Graeme Jones, Stephen Purches, Simon Weatherstone, Dan Hodges, Andy Howe and Jordan Tribe for their incredible loyalty, support and dedication and to all of the amazing staff behind the scenes whose hard work and loyalty makes this club what it is.

‌



“A special thank you to all of the players who have represented the club during my time here. Without you, nothing would have been possible and it’s been an honour to have coached you all.

“Finally, and most importantly, thank you to our incredible supporters. Your passion and loyalty have inspired me every single day. To stand on the touchline at St. James’ Park as your manager with the honour of representing your club has meant more to me than you will ever know.

“While my journey as manager has now come to an end, the affinity and love I will always hold for Newcastle United never will.

‌



“Thank you for everything. I wish the club every success for the future.”

Matthias Jaissle, 38, is expected to become the next Newcastle manager having previously coached Saudi Arabian side Al-Ahli, who he guided to two Asian Cup titles, the continent's version of the Champions League.

Sports.title: Bookies ‘run out of cash’ at Wolverhampton after favourite lands £50,000 gamble
Sports.content:
Bookies ‘run out of cash’ at Wolverhampton after favourite lands £50,000 gamble

The victory of 2-1 chance Iconic Times, trained by Jennie Candlish, was claimed to have cost racecourse bookmakers £50,000 when winning at the all-weather meeting

View 2 Images Bookmakers allegedly ran out of cash at Wolverhampton (Image: wolverhampton-racecourse.co.uk)

Bookmakers ‘ran out of cash’ at Wolverhampton on Thursday night after a heavily backed favourite landed a monumental gamble. Division one of the Download the Raceday Ready App Handicap was a lowly Class 6 race over 7f contested by 12 runners.

‌



But punters at the track only wanted to back one horse, the Jennie Candlish-trained Iconic Times. In four runs since joining the stable his nearest finish had been sixth over a mile at Southwell in April. He had finished tenth on his previous start when he went off a 28-1 chance.

‌



This time he opened at odds of 3-1 and was returned the 2-1 favourite after hitting the front a furlong out and running out the length winner. Local layer Barry Pinnington, who trades as Pinno, was reporting updates from the track on social media.

‌



Danny Mullins fined £2,500 for conduct near crowd on fractious Willie Mullins horse READ MORE :

Rising star jockey makes history by completing huge Galway Festival double READ MORE :

His first post said: “Massive gamble on course here @WolvesRaces. Fortunes for Iconic Times 25k plus.”

After the race he said: “8 books in the ring, I paid out 8k, others paid out a lot more.”

He added: “First bet in my book was a 1000 at 7/1. My colleagues were laying thousands at 5/2 just before the off. I’m amazed there were enough readies in the ring to pay out

‌



“Such a shame there is no proper betting or show reports from the ring these days. The post reports that on the 7th race at Wolves the winner opened 3/1 touched 10/3 returned 2/1. The truth is it opened 7/1 on the track and good money was laid. Bring back the on course reporters.”

View 2 Images Jennie Candlish: trainer of Iconic Times (Image: RACINGFOTOS.COM)

John Hutchinson from BDC Racing told the Racing Post, "It was a monumental gamble and quite an expensive night.

‌



"Never before have I seen every bookmaker run out of cash on a racecourse, but they did last night. That's how bad it was."

The stewards held an inquiry into the winner who “appeared to show improved form compared with its previous run at Wolverhampton on 1 June 2026 where the gelding finished tenth of 12 runners, beaten by 7 lengths.”

The report said: “Jennie Candlish’s representative’s explanation that ICONIC TIMES had benefitted from the reapplication of cheekpieces, was noted. The gelding was routine tested.”

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
