World.title: Tech firm Nebius hiring push fuels speculation over Estonia data center plans
World.content:
The international technology company Nebius, which develops artificial intelligence infrastructure, is recruiting employees in Tallinn, but the company's exact plans in Estonia are not known.

Nebius, an international technology company born from the restructuring of the Russian tech giant Yandex and headquartered in Amsterdam, is hiring in Estonia. The company is offering positions for a data centre IT manager, IT technician, IT support unit manager, IT infrastructure engineer and senior IT technician, and is also looking for a warehouse and logistics specialist.

Both Estonia's largest data centre Greenergy Data Centers and Sunly, which is building a data centre in Läänemaa, believe that if one major international client can be attracted to Estonia, others will gradually follow.

Since it became known this week that Greenergy Data Centers in Hüüru is building additional IT capacity to install artificial intelligence computing power and expand its client base beyond Estonia, journalists asked Greenergy whether they had struck a deal with Nebius.

Greenergy andmekeskus Hüürus. Autor/allikas: Tõnu Tunnel/Greenergy

Greenergy Data Centers' large‑client segment manager Martin Rungi did not wish to comment on the assumption, but noted that Greenergy has so far built out only a small part of its resource and that there is still a long way to go to reach the full potential of up to 300 megawatts.

"We are targeting all the names you hear in the public information space – Amazon, Microsoft, Google, they are all welcome clients. But who and when and in what volume will move here, that will be clear when the time is right. I cannot answer this question otherwise, but our ambition is to serve everyone operating in this field," Rungi said.

He added that the international market is highly supply‑constrained and Estonia has resources to offer. However, concrete agreements in this business are often not discussed publicly.

"A lot of things in our business are confidential until the parties themselves disclose them," Rungi said. "Since most clients are listed companies, they have their own rules for disclosure, and we cannot say anything until they are able to comment."

Nebius also did not provide clarification on its plans in Estonia.

Some data centre clients in Estonia will remain unknown to the public. For critical infrastructure, clients aim to keep the location of their data strictly hidden. Rungi said Greenergy is negotiating with many clients simultaneously and work is very active.

"There are always all kinds of speculations," Rungi said, adding that in this industry it is normal that information is disclosed only when a major client announces something.

Sunly kavandab Eestisse Baltimaade suurimat andmekeskust. Autor/allikas: Sunly

Sunly also actively seeks major clients

Commenting on Nebius hiring in Estonia, Rungi said that there are several development projects in Estonia, including Greenergy, Sunly and Evecon. "There is more than one bride at this wedding," he added.

Sunly, a renewable energy company planning to build the largest data centre in the Baltics in Läänemaa, did not wish to speculate on whether Nebius might target Greenergy's Hüüru data centre as a location.

Sunly's energy centre development manager Kaarel Aus said the sector is developing rapidly. He said Sunly is also actively negotiating with potential partners.

"The need for new data centres among major technology companies is large. A few years ago, Scandinavia and Finland were not preferred destinations for data centres. Since Western and Central European electricity grids have no short‑term capacity left for new data centres, attention has shifted to Scandinavia and Finland. Now those grids are also filling up, and data centres are looking for new locations," Aus explained.

According to Rungi, the moment when Greenergy can announce the addition of a major client may come very soon, but it may also take time.

"Sometimes where there is smoke, there is no fire, but sometimes there is," he said, adding that more than one good piece of news is coming. "Our industry is such that first we lay the egg and then we cackle."

Nebius' origins are linked to Yandex

Nebius may raise questions due to its connection to the Russian technology company Yandex, as Nebius emerged after Yandex came under sanctions following Russia's full‑scale invasion of Ukraine.

In 2024, the company sold its Russian business units and adopted the name Nebius Group, headquartered in the Netherlands. Nebius CEO Arkady Volozh is one of Yandex's founders, but he has since renounced Russian citizenship.

Rungi said Nebius is being labelled with things that are not true and that it is likely the most thoroughly scrutinised organisation in the entire chain.

"Because they were once connected to Russia, their burden is so heavy that it is even harder to gain trust. Yet they have earned trust from Meta, Microsoft, the US government, Nvidia and the New York Stock Exchange," he said. "I do not understand why this labelling continues."

Shared data hall equipment racks. Source: Tõnu Tunnel/Greenergy

Greenergy has operated for ten years, the first five spent on preparation, and has since offered services to the Estonian market while also investing in international expansion. A concern is Estonia's proximity to Russia, which causes hesitation among many potential foreign clients.

"At the same time, Finland has gained clients from this world and is also a neighbour of Russia (Nebius will build one of Europe's largest AI data centres in Finland by 2028). It is also about reputation, reliability, being known and trusted," Rungi said, adding that Greenergy has held hundreds of client meetings and practically all technology companies targeted by market players have visited them.

Aus said geopolitics is always part of negotiations with potential partners, but Estonia's membership in NATO and the European Union reduces risks for foreign partners.

Data centers could make a strong contribution to Estonia's GDP

If one major international client can be attracted to Estonia, finding additional clients will become much easier, Rungi said.

"This is a gravity business. If one comes, others follow. That is how it goes internationally; I have seen this pattern in many new markets. First come some crazy guys like us with an ambitious plan to do something that supposedly can never happen. Until the first breakthrough comes and the market develops," he said.

Aus agreed: once one major player establishes itself in the Baltics, validating the region as a data centre location, others will start looking more seriously, as has happened in Scandinavia and Finland.

"If we delay too long, until Western Europe's electricity grids catch up with demand, we will lose the opportunity to attract data centres here," Aus said.

Success, however, is hard‑won. Rungi said other countries offer tax incentives for such businesses, but Estonia does not, and there is no support from the export promotion system. He said established players are supported, but new ones do not qualify even when their ambitions are large and they have invested significant capital.

Data centres could bring substantial benefits to the state as a new economic sector. Rungi said that if Estonia's full potential were used, consuming local electricity and adding value through expertise, it would mean billions of euros annually in additional revenue for electricity companies and rental income for data centres, contributing a significant share to Estonia's GDP. The prerequisite is public acceptance.

Rungi said AI tends to be demonised, and although there are contexts where criticism is justified, accusations that data centres are to blame for energy consumption are unfair. He stressed that they do not consume energy for nothing – demand arises when people pay with a bank card or watch a film on Netflix.

"Just as a landfill is not to blame for the creation of waste, but people are, the same applies in the digital information space," he said. "We have a long way to go to make this clear."

He added that high water consumption in data centres is true in hot climates, but at Estonia's latitude, cooling is needed only for a small number of hours per year, which is a competitive advantage.

"The climate allows for much more efficient business, and in the end that means money," Rungi said.

Aus noted that Estonia currently has practically no energy‑intensive industry. For example, electricity consumption per capita in Norway is nearly four times higher than in Estonia, and in Sweden and Finland it is twice as high.

World.title: Estonian FA boss on FIFA privatization plan: The sport should be for football people
World.content:
Pohlak and EJL secretary general Mihkel Uiboleht took part in a UEFA online meeting held on an extraordinary basis on Thursday afternoon to form a common position on FIFA's plans.

"For Europe's football associations, FIFA's plan raises three main concerns. First, governance – decision-making in football can only be in the hands of football people. Second, the process – not a single association, confederation or other stakeholder was involved in developing the plan. Third, money – there is no need to involve private investors to provide additional support to members, thereby opening the door to money flowing out of football. FIFA has already earned this money by organizing various competitions and will continue to do so in the future. At today's meeting, we fully supported what was set out in UEFA's joint statement," Pohlak said after the meeting.

In the official statement issued after the meeting, UEFA unequivocally rejected FIFA's proposal to allow private investors to acquire stakes in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions.

An official statement followed, in which FIFA said the World Cup "is not for sale."

Statement on behalf of UEFA and its 55 National Associations — UEFA (@UEFA) July 30, 2026

"UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA's proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors," the statement read.

"The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football's greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams, and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale," the statement went on.

FIFA says it will continue consulting member associations on its proposal to sell up to a 20 percent stake in a new company that would manage the World Cup and other major tournaments. UEFA has threatened to boycott FIFA competitions over the plan, arguing it risks the future of football, while other confederations have also raised concerns. FIFA insists no decision will be made without member approval and denies it is "selling football."

FIFA boss Gianni Infantino says the process will represent the "democratization" of football. Many of the private investors are reportedly connected to associates of US President Donald Trump, whose close relationship with Infantino was extensively reported on during the recent World Cup in North America.

World.title: EDF intel: Shipping from Ukraine's ports halted after Russian attacks
World.content:
Shipping from Ukraine's ports in the Odesa region has come to a "complete halt" after Russian attacks, as owners are not willing to let their vessels enter ports, the Estonian Defense Forces Intelligence Center has said.

The main developments of the war this week have been the worsening of relations between Ukraine and Iran after a Ukrainian drone hit an Iranian cargo ship, as well as intense mutual medium- and long-range precision strikes between Ukraine and Russia, the Estonian Defense Forces Intelligence Center said in its weekly overview.

Worsening relations between Ukraine and Iran

The intelligence Center said a noteworthy development was Iran's statement following a Ukrainian drone attack on an Iranian merchant vessel in the Caspian Sea.

While tensions were reduced during a phone call with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, he still said that Ukraine must compensate for the damage caused by the attack.

During the war, Iran has supplied Russia with drone technology, missiles, ammunition and other equipment, and together with Russia, North Korea and China is among the countries that are highly interested in dismantling the current world order, the Intelligence Center said.

"Iran's missile arsenal makes it capable of attacking Ukraine," it emphasized.

Ukraine ports at a standstill after Russian strikes

The agency also highlighted Russia's attacks on Ukraine's ports in the Odesa region, which have brought shipping to a "complete halt" since July 22. Ukraine has raised the situation at a meeting of the UN Security Council.

"The situation is serious because Ukraine exports 90 percent of its agricultural products through Black Sea ports. Officially, shipping has not been suspended, but many shipowners do not allow their vessels to enter Ukrainian ports," the intelligence agency's statement said.

"As ships are not transporting grain out of the ports, Ukraine has also restricted the movement of grain-loaded trains to Odesa. To offset the disruption of maritime transport, Ukraine is implementing measures to export agricultural products by rail, but its lower capacity does not fully compensate for the halt in maritime transport."

Fuel shortages reach Russia's front line

The overview also touched on Ukraine's long-range strikes on the Wildberries warehouses and fuel infrastructure across Russia, as well as the Avitek military plant in the Kirov region.

"According to various estimates, Ukraine's attacks on Russia's fuel industry have reduced Russia's oil refining capacity by 20–40 percent, and reports have also emerged publicly of fuel shortages in Russian Armed Forces units fighting in Ukraine," the intellegence center said.

Ukrainian President Zelenskyy has presented plans to further increase the range of long-range strikes and to attack targets that have so far remained beyond reach but are important for Russia's continuation of the war against Ukraine, it added

World.title: Narva‑Jõesuu begins demolition of local ghost town
World.content:
In Ida‑Viru County, demolition has begun on the derelict apartment blocks of Viivikonna village, Estonia's best‑known ghost town. Narva‑Jõesuu plans to turn the abandoned mining settlement into a district of neat residential homes. Tourism operators, however, hope at least some of the old buildings will be preserved.

Just a few years ago, Viivikonna attracted tourists, musicians and filmmakers who used the empty buildings as shooting locations. Today, most houses along the main street have already disappeared.

Viivikonna was transferred to Narva-Jõesuu from Kohtla‑Järve during the administrative reform. Narva‑Jõesuu began tearing down the derelict blocks with the aim of transforming the area into a respectable neighbourhood of private homes.

"The next stage is cleaning up the plots, dividing them and selling them. The area has entirely new potential," said Narva‑Jõesuu Mayor Maksim Iljin.

Maksim Iljin. Autor/allikas: ERR

Tourism operators in Ida‑Virumaa are divided. Some say the region still has plenty of Soviet‑era heritage; others see the destruction of Ida‑Viru's uniqueness.

"We're losing the distinctive, sometimes extreme sights that define Ida‑Virumaa. What's happening now is simply erasing a chapter of history. Soon we'll have only empty lots that quickly become overgrown," said Marko Kaldur, guide at avastaEesti.ee.

Kaldur noted that a film studio complex is currently being built in Ida‑Virumaa, but by the time it is ready, potential filming locations may already be gone.

The mayor acknowledges receiving requests from tourism operators and filmmakers to preserve Viivikonna's ghost buildings, but none are willing to take responsibility for safety and maintenance.

"Of course, for us it's a constant headache, and honestly — from the beginning we saw no real future for these apartment blocks. In my view, demolition is the most sensible option," Iljin said.

Narva‑Jõesuu estimates that clearing Viivikonna of derelict buildings will cost around €1 million, most of which will be covered by state support.

World.title: Turnover volume of grocery stores up in June after long decline
World.content:
Retail sales turnover rose to €950 million in June – an increase of 1 percent on year – bucking a more than two-year negative trend, data from Statistics Estonia shows.

Johanna Linda Pihlak, a leading analyst at Statistics Estonia, pointed out that the turnover volume of retail trade enterprises, which had declined in May, began to grow again in June.

The increase in turnover volume in June was driven by grocery stores, which saw turnover volume grow after more than two years of decline.

"The last time the turnover volume of grocery stores grew was in March 2024," she said.

Turnover volume index. Source: Statistics Estonia

The turnover volume of both enterprises engaged in the retail sale of automotive fuel and stores selling manufactured goods remained at the level of June 2025.

"In the case of enterprises engaged in the retail sale of automotive fuel, it is worth noting that the data covers not only the sale of motor fuels but reflects total sales, including income from food service and provision of other goods and services," the analyst added.

Compared with May, the turnover volume of retail trade enterprises increased by 2 percent in June. According to seasonally and working-day adjusted data, turnover volume was up by one percent compared to the previous month.

In the first half of this year, the retail trade turnover increased by three percent compared with the same period of the previous year.

World.title: Iraq denies launching strikes from its territory against neighboring nations
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The military spokesperson for the Iraqi commander-in-chief, Sabah al-Numan, confirmed on Thursday that neither a foreign nor local body has presented proof that recent regional drone attacks were launched from Iraqi territory.

In a statement to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), al-Numan urged accusing parties to submit reliable proof, saying that Baghdad has yet to receive such data.

The development comes following statements made by the Saudi Ministry of Defense, alleging that drone attacks targeting key oil infrastructure in the past few days originated in Iraq.

The Iraqi official indicated that the government will neither tolerate unilateral military acts from within its borders nor accept foreign violations of its territorial sovereignty.

Al-Numan’s remarks come a day after the United States and Saudi Arabia launched coordinated airstrikes targeting several bases of Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), killing and injuring many fighters.

The joint operation targeted several logistical and weapons storage locations in different provinces in Iraq, escalating the current regional battle.

The PMF described the joint US-Saudi strike as a dangerous escalation and a clear breach of Iraqi sovereignty.

World.title: Iraqi oil flows to continue via Turkey’s Ceyhan as renewal deal is discussed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkish sources told Reuters that crude oil shipments from northern Iraq to the Turkish port of Ceyhan will continue while the two countries seek an arrangement to extend the pipeline’s operation for another 12 months.

On July 27, a bilateral agreement that had been in place for decades ended. Despite expectations, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi did not sign a 12-month renewal deal during his meeting with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Ankara on Tuesday.

According to a Turkish official, oil flows via the Iraq-Turkey pipeline, which is Baghdad’s only operational export pipeline, will continue while negotiations for a renewal deal are still in progress.

Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar recently announced a 12-month extension agreement between the two countries.

During a joint press conference in Ankara, Erdogan stated on Tuesday that Turkey hopes to finalize a comprehensive energy cooperation agreement as soon as possible.

An extension is intended to provide additional time for discussions on a complete accord. Turkey aims to fully utilize the 1.5 million barrels per day pipeline and consider expanding it to oil fields in southern Iraq.

Turkish data suggests that the pipeline currently transports approximately 170,000 barrels per day.

World.title: Turkey seeks comprehensive energy cooperation deal with Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan stated that Turkey hopes to finalize a comprehensive energy cooperation agreement with Iraq following discussions with Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi in Ankara.

Erdogan said that Turkey’s state-owned oil and gas company, TPAO, will operate at Iraq’s Kirkuk oilfield, which is now being developed by British Petroleum (BP), during a joint press conference following a signing ceremony that had been expected to extend the Kirkuk-Ceyhan oil pipeline deal for another year, according to Reuters.

The agreement to renew the decades-old pipeline contract, which regulates shipments along the strategic route, expired on Monday.

After signing three agreements, Erdogan noted that additional deals were anticipated. However, his ministers promptly briefed him on stage, and the two leaders continued with their statements without announcing any further agreements.

The agreement between Iraq and Turkey regarding the crude oil pipeline expired on July 27.

“Our goal is to complete an energy cooperation deal that benefits both parties as quickly as possible,” Erdogan said.

Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar said in a statement on X that TPAO has bought a 15 percent stake in BP Energy Company of Kirkuk Limited (BPECKL), enabling the Turkish business to operate in the sector.

Bayraktar explained the TPAO will cooperate with BPECKL to raise oil production at the Kirkuk field, which has reserves estimated at three million barrels.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports to India fall as New Delhi diversifies import sources
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi oil exports to India fell in the first half of 2026, as Indian refineries diversified their crude import sources to minimize the geopolitical risks associated with shipping via the Straits of Hormuz.

According to officials at Indian refining companies and the Indian Ministry of Petroleum, the goal of this measure is to improve supply security.

The drop in Iraqi supplies to India comes at a time when the global oil market is under increased pressure due to security worries along critical maritime routes. This pressure is causing consumers in Asia to split their purchases among many producing countries.

Iraqi oil remains a vital resource for India due to supply security and the high quality of Basra crude.

Indian refiners confirmed they have secured their crude oil requirements until the end of September and have begun arranging purchases for the fourth quarter of the year, despite persistent concerns about the impact of any interruptions to shipping routes on global supply chains.

Meanwhile, Russia remained India’s top crude oil supplier in the first half of the year, while imports from the UAE and Brazil increased.

India’s purchases from Iraq and the United States fell as New Delhi attempted to diversify its supply sources and reduce the risks associated with reliance on a single source.

Indian refiners have warned that increased shipping risks and higher insurance costs, along with declining discounts on Russian oil, are affecting profit margins.

Experts anticipate that continuing instability in the Middle East will raise oil prices and pose new hurdles for Asian oil-importing countries.

World.title: Six Iranian advisors killed in US-Saudi attack on Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A joint US-Saudi attack on targets in Iraq killed six Iranian advisors on Wednesday, according to two Iraqi officials who spoke to the Associated Press (AP).

A meeting that was set for Thursday in Saudi Arabia between Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman was called off due to recent attacks by armed groups targeting Saudi Arabia.

Al-Zaidi ordered an emergency meeting of Iraq’s National Security Council following the coordinated attacks on the country.

The Iraqi Security Media Cell said in a statement that the meeting was ordered in response to the evolving security situation and the airstrikes that targeted several Iraqi provinces early on Wednesday.

The US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced on Wednesday that US forces, in cooperation with Saudi armed forces, carried out precision airstrikes targeting sites linked to Iran-backed militias in Iraq.

The coordinated airstrikes were in retaliation for a series of drone attacks targeting US interests and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

CENTCOM said in a statement that the strikes, carried out on July 28, targeted logistics sites and weapons depots allegedly used by Iranian-backed groups. It added that these groups were directed by the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) to attack US forces and Saudi oil facilities.

US and Saudi fighter jets carried out the strikes, an operation described by CENTCOM as a strong response to more than 30 drone attacks that the IRGC had conducted in the past few days.

Headquarters and sites belonging to the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) in several Iraqi provinces were targeted by the US-Saudi airstrikes in the country.

World.title: US-Saudi strikes test Iraq’s fragile security balance
World.content:
Baghdad – US-Saudi strikes on Iraq killed at least 20 militants, including several Iranians, on Wednesday, according to the Hashed al-Shaabi, an armed Iraqi alliance that includes pro-Iran groups.

The United States and Saudi Arabia said they had struck Iran-backed armed militants in Iraq in response to attacks on US forces and Saudi oil facilities.

Washington and Tehran are Iraq’s main allies, but their enmity has long turned the country into a proxy battleground and left successive governments struggling to maintain a delicate balance between the foes.

The Hashed al-Shaabi, also known as the Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF), said that at least 20 fighters “were martyred and another 32 wounded according to a preliminary toll”.

Two Hashed officials told AFP that five Iranian advisors were among those killed in a strike in the central province of Diyala.

AFP correspondents saw coffins wrapped in Iranian flags during a funeral organised by the Hashed al-Shaabi in Baghdad for those killed.

The Hashed alliance was created in 2014 to fight jihadists before it was formally integrated into the Iraqi armed forces.

It now includes brigades belonging to Iran-backed groups reputed for acting unilaterally.

US President Donald Trump said the strikes were coordinated with the Iraqi government, according to Fox News.

They follow growing US pressure on Baghdad to disarm pro-Iran armed groups, which have frequently targeted US facilities in the country and have long called for the withdrawal of US troops.

Iraq’s new Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, who came to power this year with Washington’s blessing, vowed to ensure those groups would hand over their weapons, but has faced pushback from some powerful factions.

Earlier this month, Zaidi visited both the United States and Iran.

– ‘Inevitable response’ –

The strikes came after Riyadh said its forces had intercepted drones targeting oil facilities, blaming the Iran-backed groups in Iraq.

The most active pro-Iran armed groups are united under an alliance known as the Islamic Resistance in Iraq, which has acted in support of Tehran during the Middle East war, claiming hundreds of attacks against US bases in Iraq and across the region.

The Islamic Resistance in Iraq said “our response to the American enemy is inevitable, and may target its tools in Saudi Arabia”.

But the group added that it would only retaliate after the Arbaeen day of pilgrimage, which falls on Tuesday.

The Arbaeen marks one of the most significant events in the Shia Muslim calendar, during which pilgrims, many from Iran, flock to Iraq to visit the holy shrines.

The pro-Iran groups denied attacking Saudi Arabia and they haven’t claimed any attacks since the US-Iran war resumed earlier this month.

– Violation –

Iraq denounced the US-Saudi strikes and said it rejects “all acts of aggression, regardless of the party responsible or the justifications presented.”

The Ministerial Council for National Security said it would “confront any violation of Iraq’s sovereignty, and prevent any source from using Iraqi territory to threaten neighbouring states”.

It reaffirmed its commitment to ensure the state’s monopoly over weapons.

Zaidi’s government has given those groups that Washington designates as terrorist organisations until September 30 to disarm.

Oil-rich Iraq has been trying to move past decades of war and unrest, but it remains vulnerable to regional and internal flare-ups.

World.title: Iraq condemns US-Saudi strikes, vows tighter control over armed groups
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq condemned U.S.-Saudi airstrikes on Wednesday that targeted Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) sites, calling the attacks a violation of its sovereignty, and announced new measures to tighten state control over security and prevent Iraqi territory from being used to threaten neighboring countries.

Following the attacks, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi presided over an emergency meeting of the Ministerial Council for National Security, which the government said killed and injured many Iraqis.

As regional tensions rose, Al-Zaidi cancelled a planned visit to Saudi Arabia on Thursday.

In a statement published after the meeting, the council said that the strikes happened when Baghdad was already in talks with US and Saudi authorities over suspicions that Iran-aligned armed organizations operating from Iraq committed drone assaults on Saudi land.

“The government was actively engaging with the relevant parties to verify and address the concerns raised by both the Saudi and US sides,” the statement stated, adding that the military action hampered such efforts.

The council authorized a comprehensive security strategy aimed at strengthening state authority across Iraq, combating breaches of Iraqi sovereignty, and prohibiting any party from exploiting Iraqi territory to threaten neighboring nations.

The steps reflect Baghdad’s efforts to guarantee that no armed organization may launch assaults from Iraqi soil that could pull the nation into larger regional wars, while also confirming the government’s goal of bringing all security actions under state control.

The council also directed the Foreign Ministry to take legal and diplomatic measures under international law and the United Nations Charter to record the attacks and protect Iraq’s legal rights.

The government condemned the attacks but emphasized that responding to security threats and enforcing the law is solely the responsibility of Iraq’s constitutional institutions.

“The government rejects all acts of aggression, regardless of the party responsible or the justifications presented,” the statement read.

The council underlined Baghdad’s commitment to addressing regional conflicts via diplomacy while maintaining efforts to keep all armaments under state control.

It also restated Iraq’s commitment to carrying out the security agreement guiding the departure of the US-led international coalition by the end of September 2026.

The emergency conference occurred hours after US President Donald Trump claimed that the midnight attacks were coordinated with the Iraqi government, something Baghdad has not officially verified.

Iraqi authorities have openly opposed the operation, emphasizing the political sensitivity of the attacks.

The events highlight Al-Zaidi’s increasingly precarious situation, as he seeks to boost Iraq’s connections with the US and Gulf Arab governments while retaining relations with Iran.

His decision to cancel the Saudi visit underlines the gravity of the problem, as Baghdad seeks to temper regional tensions while preventing Iraqi land from becoming a battlefield for opposing forces.

The government’s current security strategy also suggests a renewed desire to prevent armed groups from operating outside official control, as Baghdad wants to reassure neighboring nations that Iraq will not be used as a springboard for assaults that endanger regional peace.

World.title: Uptime Institute partners with T964 to expand Iraq’s digital infrastructure
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Uptime Institute, based in the United States, and Iraqi digital infrastructure company Tech964 Holding Limited (T964) have formed a strategic partnership to help develop Iraq’s digital infrastructure, marking the latest technology agreement to result from Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s investment-focused visit to Washington.

The agreement, signed earlier this month at the U.S.-Iraq Business Summit hosted by the US Chamber of Commerce, names T964 as Uptime Institute’s business partner in Iraq to promote international data center standards, professional training, and the development of resilient digital infrastructure.

The agreement is part of Baghdad’s larger effort to diversify its economy beyond oil by increasing digital infrastructure, attracting technological investment, and bolstering industries including cloud computing, artificial intelligence, financial technology, and cybersecurity.

T964, one of Iraq’s major private digital infrastructure businesses, has announced that it would collaborate with the Uptime Institute to implement internationally recognized standards for the country’s expanding network of data centers, as well as increase technical competence and operational best practices.

The partnership is anticipated to help establish carrier-neutral data centers, telecommunications infrastructure, cloud services, and AI-ready digital platforms, all of which the government believes are important to modernizing public services and stimulating private-sector investment.

The pact follows a series of technological ties announced during Al-Zaidi’s tour to the United States, during which Iraq inked more than 50 agreements totaling more than $60 billion in the energy, banking, infrastructure, industrial, and technology sectors.

Improving digital infrastructure has become a key component of Iraq’s long-term economic plan, as the country strives to lessen reliance on oil earnings and establish a knowledge-based economy capable of attracting foreign technology businesses while also encouraging homegrown innovation.

The alliance also underscores increased US private-sector interest in Iraq’s digital economy, especially as demand for secure data centers, cloud computing capacity, and AI infrastructure in the Middle East grows.

Iraq has increasingly prioritized digital infrastructure for foreign investment alongside energy and transportation, with officials claiming that internationally certified data centers and modern telecommunications networks will be critical to supporting e-government services, digital banking, e-commerce, and artificial intelligence, as well as strengthening Iraq’s role as an emerging regional technology hub.

World.title: Chhattisgarh worker shot dead, another wounded in first J&K terror attack on migrants in 21 months
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Terrorists shot dead a 24-year-old labourer from Chhattisgarh and critically wounded another from the same state at a brick kiln in south Kashmirâs Kulgam on Friday evening, marking the first fatal attack on migrant workers in J&K since unidentified assailants killed a native of Biharâs Banka in Shopian district on Oct 18, 2024.

IGP (Kashmir) Vidhi Kumar Birdi identified the slain worker as Deepak Ratray. His wounded co-worker, Bhupender (28), has been moved to Government Medical College in Anantnag.

The last such terror strike targeting migrant labourers in Kulgam was on Oct 11, 2021, when two men from Bihar, Raja Reshi Dev and Joginder Reshi Dev, were killed in their rented accommodation in Wanpoh.

âI strongly condemn this cowardly act. I have directed our security forces to step up their operations and eliminate the terrorists,â lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha wrote on X, adding that he had spoken to DGP Nalin Prabhat and other top security officials.

PDP chief and ex-CM Mehbooba Mufti said it was a shame that workers migrating to find employment had been targeted. âThey work themselves to the bone far away from home only to feed their families. Unimaginably cruel to target them in such senseless acts of violence,â she said.

World.title: Delhi riots: Convicts' kin to challenge life sentence in HC, deny links to Tahir Hussain
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The family of two convicts sentenced to life imprisonment in the Ankit Sharma murder case, along with former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain, on Friday said they would challenge the trial court's verdict in the Delhi High Court.

Speaking to ANI, Mohammad Asif, the brother of convicts Nazim and Kasim, claimed that his brothers had been falsely implicated in the case and denied any connection with Tahir Hussain.

"We will appeal in the High Court. One of my brothers, the younger one, Kasim, lived in the village. The other one too had gone to the village two days before the incident. Tahir Hussain's house is very far away; we had no connection at all," Asif said.

Alleging police misconduct, he added, "The police brought them in and filed a case against them."

Meanwhile, speaking to ANI over the phone, Ankit's brother, Ankur Sharma, said, "Our demand was that the court should treat this case as a 'rarest of rare' case, and that the guilty should receive the harshest possible punishment. They should have been given the death penalty; that is what we wanted."

"As the case moves to the Delhi High Court or the Supreme Court, we want my brother to get justice there as well, and the guilty should receive the severest punishment. An example should be set so that such an incident never happens to anyone else," he added.

The court has awarded life imprisonment to all five convicts. The prosecution had argued that Sharma suffered 51 injuries and was brutally assaulted before his body was dumped into a drain.

World.title: 'Muslims can't regard country as deity': Islamic body objects to Vande Mataram Bill
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

(AIMPLB) on Friday strongly criticised Parliamentâs passage of a Bill that makes alleged disrespect to Vande Mataram a punishable offence, calling it an attack on religious and constitutional freedoms and urging the government not to impose patriotic expressions through legal compulsion.

In a press release issued on 31 July, the Muslim body said the legislation was contrary to the constitutional, secular and democratic ethos of the country and amounted to a serious assault on the religious freedom of citizens. It argued that compelling participation in a song or slogan carrying religious connotations violated fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution.

The Boardâs spokesperson, Dr SQR Ilyas, said that making Vande Mataram legally mandatory for all communities was incompatible with both constitutional principles and Islamic belief.

âAny attempt to make Vande Mataram compulsory for all sections and religious communities through legal coercion is not only objectionable but also contrary to the fundamental principles of the Constitution,â he said.

The AIMPLB said that during the framing of the Constitution, the Constituent Assembly accepted only the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram at the national level, while the religious connotations of the remaining portions were not considered compatible with Indiaâs secular character.





Dr Ilyas argued that certain passages of the song depict the motherland in the form of a goddess and exhort people to worship her, which he said was contrary to the Islamic doctrine of Tawheed, or the absolute Oneness of God.

âTherefore, compelling a Muslim to participate in a song, slogan or practice carrying a religious meaning contrary to his or her faith is wholly unacceptable,â he said.

The Board also cited Articles 25 and 19 of the Constitution, saying they protect the freedom of religion and freedom of expression, including the right not to participate in expressions that conflict with an individualâs conscience.

âThese constitutional safeguards clearly imply that no citizen can be compelled to adopt or participate in any song, slogan, ideology or symbol against his or her religious beliefs and conscience,â the statement said.

Referring to the Supreme Courtâs landmark judgment in Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala, Dr Ilyas said the court had upheld this principle even in the context of the national anthem.

âThe Court held that a person could not be punished merely for not participating in an act when doing so was contrary to his or her religious beliefs.

The Court also made it clear that, in certain circumstances, freedom of expression includes the right to remain silent, and that respectful non-participation cannot be regarded as disrespect.â

The AIMPLB sought to distinguish between patriotism and religious devotion, saying that love for oneâs country should not be equated with worship.

âLove for the motherland and worship of the motherland are two entirely different concepts.

Muslims deeply love their country and consider love for the homeland part of their civic and moral responsibility, but they cannot regard the country as a deity or goddess.â

The Board added that patriotism should be judged by a citizenâs commitment to the Constitution, the countryâs people and their rights rather than by the recitation of a particular slogan or song.

It also urged the government to prioritise issues such as unemployment, inflation, poverty, education, healthcare, economic inequality and social injustice instead of pursuing what it described as sensitive and divisive measures.

âDiverting public attention from fundamental issues by inflaming emotional and religious controversies serves neither the national interest nor the cause of democracy.â

Concluding its statement, the AIMPLB said that Indiaâs unity could only be strengthened by protecting constitutional supremacy, religious freedom and equal rights for all citizens.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âA strong and united India can only be built where every citizen enjoys equal dignity, justice and freedom; where anyoneâs patriotism is not judged through the prism of his or her religious beliefs; and where the supremacy of the Constitution, religious freedom and fundamental civil rights are protected at all costs.â

The Vande Matram Bill, passed by both Houses of Parliament on Friday, seeks to make alleged disrespect to Vande Mataram a punishable offence and gives legal backing to its mandatory observance in specified contexts. Supporters have described the measure as a way to promote national unity and respect for a national symbol, while critics argue that it could compel citizens to participate in patriotic expressions regardless of their religious beliefs or freedom of conscience, raising concerns over constitutional rights and religious freedom.

World.title: 'India always supportive of dialogue and diplomacy': Jaishankar speaks to Iran FM Araghchi
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India on Friday expressed deep concern over the escalating conflict in West Asia, with external affairs minister

speaking to his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi and urging restraint amid growing regional tensions.

In a post on X after the conversation, Jaishankar said he had a "tele-conversation" with Araghchi and reiterated India's concerns over the deteriorating security situation. "Conveyed our deep concerns at the ongoing hostilities in the region," he wrote.

Jaishankar also stressed the need to protect commercial shipping and seafarers as the conflict increasingly threatens key maritime routes. "Strongly urged that attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers be avoided under any circumstance.

India condemns any such attack by any party," he said.

The external affairs minister added that he was briefed on Tehran's position during the call. "Was apprised of Iranâs perspective of current developments and discussions underway. India is always supportive of dialogue and diplomacy," Jaishankar wrote.

The conversation came as tensions between Iran and the United States intensified, with Tehran claiming fresh strikes on American military facilities in Kuwait.





According to Iranian state media, the Iranian army carried out drone attacks on the US-operated Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base as part of the 27th phase of Operation Lightning. Tehran said the operation was launched in response to a recent US strike on a residential home on Qeshm Island, alleging that it targeted military infrastructure including aircraft shelters, satellite communication systems and equipment warehouses.

World.title: 'Pak-trained Mujahideen have turned their guns inwards': India slams Islamabad over PoK crackdown
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India on Friday slammed Pakistan of making an open admission of state-sponsored terrorism after a senior aide to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif acknowledged that Islamabad had trained and armed Mujahideen who have now turned against the Pakistani state.

The ministry of external affairs (MEA) also condemned Pakistan's crackdown on anti-government protesters in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK), alleging that more than 40 civilians had been killed.

Addressing the weekly media briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Pakistan's handling of the protests had exposed its treatment of civilians in the region.

"As you and all of us have witnessed, the Pakistani establishment continues to unleash ruthless force against peaceful civilians in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir.

This crackdown has resulted in the tragic death of over 40 innocent people, and many more have been seriously injured. It's the establishment's absolute disdain for the innocent people of Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir that was laid bare when their Defence Minister branded the protesting civilians as enemies," Jaiswal said.

Referring to recent remarks by Pakistan Prime Minister's Special Assistant on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Jaiswal said the statement amounted to a public acknowledgement that Pakistan had trained, funded and armed militants who were later sent into India.





"The Special Assistant of the Prime Minister [of Pakistan] on Political Affairs has openly admitted that the very Mujahideen that the Pakistani establishment trained, funded, armed, and sent to India have turned their guns inwards, weaponising themselves against the state," Jaiswal said.

The remarks came after Sanaullah, in an interview with Geo News, said: "are the same people we once trained as Mujahideen. We sent them to fight, and today they are hanging around our necks."

India has long accused Pakistan of sponsoring cross-border terrorism, an allegation Islamabad has consistently denied.

Jaiswal also criticised the recently held elections in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, calling them a rejection of Pakistan's establishment.

"The so-called elections stand as a humiliating rejection of the Pakistan establishment. Facing a violent regime, the people have requested international organisations for an independent investigation into the unlawful killings.

We urged that the international community should scrutinise Pakistan's actions and hold it accountable for its atrocities," Jaiswal said.

According to ANI, widespread protests have erupted across PoJK over allegations of electoral rigging, political interference and suppression of democratic rights.

The United Kashmir People's National Party (UKPNP) has appealed to the United Nations and the international community to intervene over what it described as a worsening human rights situation in the region.

In a statement posted on X, the organisation urged international institutions, governments and human rights organisations to take immediate steps to protect civilians, ensure accountability and uphold international human rights law.

World.title: Assam floods: Death toll rises to 80; state shifts focus to rehabilitation, announces loan relief
World.content:
Two more deaths in Sivasagar pushed Assam's flood toll to 80 on Friday, even as more than 2.12 lakh people across eight districts continued to grapple with the deluge.

The latest figures mark an improvement from the previous day's situation, when the flood toll stood at 78, over 3 lakh people across seven districts were affected, and floodwaters had inundated 551 villages and more than 21,500 hectares of crop area.

21 revenue circles and 437 villages remain inundated across Golaghat, Sivasagar, Biswanath, Charaideo, Kamrup (Metropolitan), Jorhat, Dhemaji and Nagaon. Charaideo remains the worst-hit district with nearly 80,000 affected people, followed by Sivasagar (71,000) and Jorhat (40,000), PTI cites.

Floodwaters have also caused extensive damage to embankments, roads, bridges and other public infrastructure.

Rescue teams continue relief operations

According to the recent data shared by the government, relief operations are continuing across Assam, with 216 relief camps and 1,788 relief distribution centres supporting flood-affected communities. The camps are currently sheltering 71,416 people, while authorities continue to provide food, drinking water, medicines and other essential supplies. Sarma said rehabilitation efforts remain the government's top priority as floodwaters recede.





The Army, NDRF, SDRF, Fire and Emergency Services, police and civil administration remain engaged in rescue and relief efforts.

In an X post, CM Himanta wrote, "Our teams are working 24*7 while we are formulating policies to directly benefit the affected."

With floodwaters receding, Sarma said the administration has expanded relief work to include debris clearance, doorstep healthcare, disposal of animal carcasses, disinfection drives, restoration of electricity and other essential services.

Government announces loan relief package

Chief minister

on Thursday also announced a six-month moratorium on repayment of loans availed by flood-affected people in Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat and Golaghat districts. The decision was taken at a special meeting of the State Level Bankers' Committee (SLBC), attended by representatives of the RBI, NABARD, SBI and other commercial banks.

Banks have also agreed to extend loan tenures by one to seven years, depending on the type of loan, he informed. The Assam government has sought a special relief package from the Centre and urged the Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT) to classify the Upper

as an "atypical, high-intensity, rapid-onset event" for more flexible relief norms.

Meanwhile, Assam ministers flagged off 30 trucks carrying food, clothing and other essential supplies for flood-hit districts.

Assam minister Atul Bora, talking to ANI, said the government was continuing relief operations on a war footing and highlighted the Rs 15,000 financial assistance announced for each affected family, in addition to food supplies and other necessities.

Cloudburst triggered unprecedented flooding: CM

Earlier, chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma had attributed the devastating floods to an intense cloudburst in the upstream states of Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland.

In a post on X on July 22, he said Arunachal Pradesh received 141% above-normal rainfall, while Nagaland recorded 181% above-normal precipitation, resulting in an unprecedented discharge of floodwaters into Assam.

World.title: Force of law: On the Delhi police
World.content:
The extent and the nature of police action, which continues in Delhi against student protesters, remain a matter of grave concern for India’s democracy. The Supreme Court of India is seized of the matter, but it has done little so far to restrain the police, which appears to be acting outside of the law. To have an independent inquiry that examines the allegations being raised — as is being considered by the Court — is one thing. But an accountable police force would have swiftly acted to preserve its own honour and reputation, considering what is already available in the public domain. Its male officers in uniform appear in videos slapping a woman protester, and attempting to bring down a lathi on the private parts of a girl. The Delhi police is actively pursuing protesters who were apparently present at the protest site, using facial-recognition and other surveillance technologies, the legality of which remains dubious and controversial. Yet, it has offered no response regarding the identity of the officer seen openly assaulting a young woman at a public gathering. The Delhi police would not require any software or Court intervention to identify and hold its own personnel accountable. All it needs is professionalism and a strict adherence to the principle of the rule of law.

There is also a simultaneous law-enforcement sweep against freedom of expression, both online and offline, targeting critics of the government. The police appears eager to proceed against people merely for saying something. Abusive language has indeed been used by some content creators against government functionaries. If any of that warrants police action, the applicable law should be clearly cited, and due process should be followed transparently. Instead, there are reports of arbitrary police action that appears intended more as intimidation than law enforcement, targeting protesters, their families and, in some cases, even social media platforms. At the same time, the police seem uninterested in acting against online mobs that are threatening and abusing the protesters. The Delhi police has maintained that criminals infiltrated the protests. Those involved in violence must certainly be identified and brought to justice in accordance with the law. The force has also not explained the circumstances under which pellets were fired at protesters. Police practices must adhere to established rules and standards, and any breach must be dealt with firmly. This is an occasion for both the Centre and the Court to underscore a basic constitutional principle: nobody, including the police, is above the law. The government should not appear to have gone back on its promises to the agitating students, who called off the protests once their demands were met. That would only entrench cynicism and deepen resentment among the youth who turned up in their thousands at Jantar Mantar.

World.title: Festive atmosphere prevails across Vizag
World.content:
Visakhapatnam’s waterfront came alive with sporting events, cultural performances and public celebrations on Friday as the city geared up for the inauguration of the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram on Saturday. From Beach Road to Rushikonda Blue Flag Beach, the day-long festivities drew students, sportspersons, families and tourists as the city celebrated the region’s newest aviation gateway.

The celebrations began with the Bhogapuram Airport 5K Run, organised by the Sports Authority of Andhra Pradesh (SAAP). A large number of participants took part in the run and cycling events conducted between The Park Hotel junction and Tenneti Park, with students, women, youth and amateur athletes joining the competitions.

The event also showcased emerging sporting talent. Sainik School students dominated the open boys’ running category, while trainees from the SAAP Cycling Academy in Visakhapatnam secured the top five positions in the cycling event. Students from various schools were among the leading finishers in the open girls’ category.

Visakhapatnam East MLA Velagapudi Ramakrishna Babu, SAAP Chairman A. Ravi Naidu, Joint Collector G. Vidyadhari, District Sports Development Officer June Gallyot and other officials felicitated the winners. Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Ravi Naidu said the airport represented new opportunities for North Andhra and reiterated the importance of sports in nurturing discipline, confidence and leadership among young people.

As the day progressed, Beach Road continued to attract crowds as the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) organised ‘Uttarandhra Kalalaku Rekkalu’, featuring cultural performances and a beach walk. District Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore said the airport would strengthen connectivity and open new avenues for industrial growth and employment in North Andhra. The programme marked the culmination of a week-long series of celebrations held across the region ahead of the airport’s inauguration.

In a separate event, celebrations continued at Rushikonda Blue Flag Beach, where the Tourism Department organised a curtain-raiser featuring sand sculptures, tribal dances, kolatam, cultural performances and themed selfie points centred on the airport. A sand sculpture depicting the airport, accompanied by a message thanking farmers who had given land for the project, drew the attention of visitors.

Tourism Minister Kandula Durgesh said improved connectivity through air, road, rail and sea transport would support tourism and create employment opportunities in the region.

Around 500 people attended the beach event, where performances by children and tribal artistes added colour to the celebrations, bringing to a close a day in which sport, culture and community participation converged along Visakhapatnam’s coastline ahead of the airport’s inauguration.

World.title: Youth, reported abducted, held with suspected MDMA in Kochi
World.content:
A 24-year-old man, who had been reported abducted by a group, was arrested, along with three others, with 5 grams of suspected MDMA here on Friday. The arrested are Rijoy Beckson Francis, 24, of Maradu, Binu Mohanan, 34, of Puthencruz, Parvathi V., 35, of Haripad, and Sandranjali, 25, of Panangad.

They were arrested from an apartment at Vennala by the District Anti-Narcotics Special Action Force.

Francis was nabbed by the anti-narcotics squad two days after he was reported allegedly abducted by a group from near Maradu. The Maradu police had registered a case over the alleged abduction after a food delivery person reported to the police that he saw a youth being kidnapped by a group of three people on Wednesday (July 29).

The police identified Francis from CCTV visuals recorded from the area. They said the investigation had found that Francis was allegedly abducted by an Aluva native and his accomplices following a dispute over financial dealings related to alleged drug sales. He was let off after he repaid the money owed to the group leader. The suspected MDMA seized from Francis and his friends were allegedly bought from the group, the police said. Further probe is on, they added.

World.title: ISRO calls for stronger academia-industry partnership to power future space missions
World.content:
ISRO Chairman and Secretary, Department of Space, V. Narayanan, on Friday called for closer collaboration between academia, industry and research institutions to help realise India’s ambitious space programme, including plans to establish an indigenous space station by 2035 and land Indians on the Moon by 2040.

Delivering the keynote address virtually at ISRO Academia Connect @ AU, organised by the Capacity Building Programme Office (CBPO), ISRO, in association with Andhra University College of Engineering (A), Mr. Narayanan said the century-old Andhra University had made significant contributions to the nation by producing scientists, academicians and administrators, making it an ideal partner for advancing research and innovation.

Highlighting India’s achievements in space, he said the country had become the first to achieve a successful soft landing near the Moon’s south pole through Chandrayaan-3 and added that work was under way on Chandrayaan-4 and Chandrayaan-5. “There should not be any gap between space and the common man of this country,” he said, noting that ISRO’s satellites were supporting more than 50 sectors, including telecommunications, weather forecasting, disaster management, agriculture, fisheries, water resources and border security. He said India had also developed indigenous cryogenic technology after being denied access to it by other countries.

Calling for application-oriented research, Mr. Narayanan urged universities to move beyond academic publications and develop patents, technologies and products that benefit society. He expressed confidence that the collaboration between ISRO and Andhra University would create greater opportunities for research and internships while contributing to the country’s space programme.

ISRO Scientific Secretary M. Ganesh Pillai said the event at Andhra University was the fifth edition of ISRO’s nationwide Academic Connect initiative. “Every successful space mission is built upon decades of research, innovation and academic excellence,” he said, urging universities to undertake mission-oriented research leading to technologies, prototypes and products for future space missions.

World.title: Case against Noida woman for ‘abusing’ PM moved to Delhi
World.content: NEA day after reports of an FIR registered in Noida against a woman named Ruchika Singh for “abusing” Prime Minister Narendra Modi came to light, a senior Delhi Police officer said on Friday that the case had been transferred to the Parliament Street police station for further investigation. When reached for comment, Deputy Commissioner of Police (New Delhi) Sachin Sharma said the case had not yet been handed over to them as of Friday evening. “We will decide the course of action once we get it,” he said. On Wednesday, the U.P. police registered a zero FIR , t the Expressway police station, based on a complaint by a Ghaziabad resident, Smriti Singh. The complainant alleged that Ms. Ruchika Sused “abusive and objectionable” language against Mr. Modi, thereby undermining “the dignity of the constitutional office”. She claimed that the remarks were intended to “spread hatred and disrupt public peace”. ‘Misuse of machinery’ Reacting to the development, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Saurav Das posted on X: “The misuse of criminal machinery against Ruchika Singh is unacceptable. Profanity does not attract a criminal case. The police can focus their energy elsewhere, not on a 25-year-old.” In a video statement, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke remarked, “Law should be the same for everyone. It cannot be used against the youth of the country and not against political leaders for using abusive language.” The FIR comes against the backdrop of the CJP-led protest at Jantar Mantar, which was called off on July 25 after Dharmendra Pradhan stepped down as the Union Education Minister. Since then, media clips and social media content posted by women during the 36-day protest have been circulated on social media and they have been subjected to online harassment, Harassment continues One such post on Friday by an X user identifying himself as Shashi Kumar, a co-convener of the Bharatiya Janata Party’s Uttar Pradesh social media unit, contained a video of three women and sought an FIR against them purportedly for similar “offences” as those Ms. Ruchika Sis accused of. Similarly, an X handle ‘The Jaipur Dialogues’ shared a video of All India Students’ Association national president Neha, a prominent face in the Jantar Mantar stir wwhile calling on the Bajrang Dal to “teach her a lesson”. The account has posted several photographs and videos of protesters since July 23, seeking their identification and demanding action against them. Several anonymous accounts have also shared videos and photographs of protesters, alleging that they insulted the Prime Minister, the Army or attacked police personnel during the demonstration. Personal details, including phone numbers and addresses, have been circulated in some instances, while comments under the posts contain abusive and obscene remarks. Fear of doxxing A 19-year-old protester, whose video containing critical remarks against the Centre was made public, said she had deleted her social media accounts out of fear of doxxing and threats. “IDigital rights expert Aparajita Bharti, a founding partner at TQH Consulting, said India’s laws do not specifically address doxxing despite its increasing use to target individuals online. “Dt is legally in a grey area. When it is increasingly used to harm women, they simply withdraw from the online space,” she said. Ms. Bharti added that obscene speech and illegal speech are often conflated. “You can find something offensive, but it is not necessarily illegal. If people are issuing sexual threats, those are actionable. But sharing personal information is not specifically covered under Indian laws. Cyber cells can still ask platforms to take down such content, and that remains one of the available remedies, which all depends on the actionability.”

World.title: Non-local killed, another injured in Kulgam terror attack in J&K: Police
World.content:
Suspected terrorists shot dead a non-local worker and injured another in a targeted attack in south Kashmir’s Kulgam on Friday evening (July 31, 2026). It is the second targeted attack in south Kashmir since July 22.

A top police official told The Hindu that two non-locals were fired upon in Kulgam’s Kilam. “One died (in the firing incident) and another was being operated (in a hospital),” said the senior officer.

The police could not identify the victims immediately. Officials said the injured non-local was being treated at the Government Medical College, Anantnag, “for advanced treatment”.

Preliminary reports suggested that suspected terrorists fired upon the non-locals after the sundown and escaped from the spot, taking the cover of darkness. Security forces have cordoned off the attack site and a search operation is to trace the attackers.

Suspected terrorists have begun attacking non-locals in south Kashmir after a long lull. On July 22, terrorists shot dead a policeman manning the Amarnath yatra route in Anantnag. Later, security forces rounded up 3,500 suspects and blasted two houses of the families of the active terrorists in south Kashmir.

Official sources said both the labourers were from Chhattisgarh and worked at a brick kiln.

Chhattisgarh CM Vishnu Deo Sai expressed grief over the incident. He said that treatment of the injured labourer is ongoing at the local hospital and that Necessary instructions have been issued to the officials in this regard.

कश्मीर के कुलगाम में हुए कायराना आतंकी हमले में छत्तीसगढ़ के एक श्रमिक की दुखद मृत्यु एवं एक श्रमिक के घायल होने की खबर अत्यंत पीड़ादायक है।



घायल श्रमिक का स्थानीय अस्पताल में समुचित इलाज जारी है। अधिकारियों को इस संदर्भ में आवश्यक निर्देश दिए गए हैं।



छत्तीसगढ़ सरकार पीड़ित… — Vishnu Deo Sai (@vishnudsai) July 31, 2026

J&K Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha, who is in charge of law and order, said he spoke with J&K Director General of Police Nalin Prabhat and top security officials “following the brutal terrorist attack in Kulgam in which a labourer from Chhattisgarh was killed”.

“I strongly condemn this cowardly act. I have directed our security forces to step up their operations and eliminate the terrorists. The J&K administration and the entire nation stand with the families,” he said.

The attack evoked strong condemnation from regional parties. “Unequivocally condemn the killing. They work themselves to the bone far away from home only to feed their families. Unimaginably cruel to target them in such senseless acts of violence,” said Peoples Democratic Party president Mehbooba Mufti.

J&K Apni Party president Altaf Bukhari termed the incident as “a deeply tragic and inhuman act of violence and terrorism”. He said: “Such tragic incidents shake us all. Those behind this heinous crime must be beasts to have attacked two innocent people who were here only to earn a livelihood for their families back home. I am sure the security agencies will soon nab the perpetrators so that they are brought to justice.”

BJP J&K spokesperson Altaf Thakur described the incident as a “cowardly, barbaric and inhuman act” that is “aimed at disrupting the prevailing atmosphere of peace and normalcy in J&K.”

“Such barbaric acts are an assault on humanity and on the centuries-old traditions of brotherhood and hospitality for which Kashmir is known,” he said.

Mr. Thakur said the perpetrators and those supporting them must be brought to justice without delay. “I urge the police leadership and security agencies to conduct a thorough investigation, identify every terrorist involved in this dastardly attack, dismantle the entire network behind the crime and ensure that the perpetrators face the strictest punishment under the law,” he added.

World.title: Shraddha Walkar murder case: HC refuses to set time frame for completion of trial
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Friday refused to set a timeline for the conclusion of the trial in the Shraddha Walkar murder case, observing that the proceedings against accused Aaftab Amin Poonawala were already being conducted on a day-to-day basis.

A single-judge Bench of Justice Madhu Jain was hearing a petition filed by Shraddha’s brother Shreejay Vijay Walkar, who contended that the criminal trial in the case had been pending for an inordinately long period without any justifiable reason.

The petition sought a direction to the sessions court to conclude the trial within a time frame fixed by the High Court. It also sought a direction to the trial court “not to grant unnecessary adjournments to either party except under exceptional and unavoidable circumstances recorded in writing”.

“It is clear that the trial court is making every endeavour to conclude the trial as soon as possible. No further directions are required as the trial is being conducted on a day-to-day basis,” Justice Jain remarked during the hearing.

Shraddha, who was in a live-in relationship with the accused, was allegedly strangled to death by Mr. Poonawala on May 18, 2022.

According to the 6,629-page chargesheet filed by Delhi Police, Mr. Poonawala allegedly dismembered the body of the 27-year-old call centre employee, stored the body parts in a refrigerator and disposed of them at desolate locations over several days to avoid detection. The remains were discovered later.

Counsel for the petitioner contended that the case was progressing at a tardy pace and that, at this rate, the trial was unlikely to conclude in the coming years.

Senior advocate Amit Prasad, appearing for Delhi Police, informed the court that the trial court was already taking up the case on a day-to-day basis, except on Saturdays and Sundays. He said out of more than 200 witnesses, the testimonies of 157 had already been completed.

World.title: Allahabad HC asks for two adult sisters to be brought before it in religious conversion and marriage case
World.content:
: The Allahabad High Court has ordered the Uttar Pradesh police and the father of two adult sisters to present them before the court on August 6. The case involves allegations that the women were illegally confined after they chose to convert to Islam and marry partners of their own choice.

The order was passed by Justice Sandeep Jain on July 30 while hearing a petition filed by Divya Bhatia (now Zoya Diya Bhatia), 20, and Anshu Bhatia (now Amina Anshu Bhatia), 35.

The sisters, through their counsel, informed the court that they voluntarily converted from Hinduism to Islam without any pressure, force, or inducement. They also said they had decided to marry according to their own wishes, which they argued is their constitutional right as adults.

According to the counsel for the women, their father, Anil Kumar Bhatia, filed a police complaint in Agra in May 2025 to stop them from making these choices. It is further alleged that, with the help of local police, they were being illegally confined because they acted against their father’s wishes.

The lawyer for the sisters argued that the Uttar Pradesh Prohibition of Unlawful Conversion of Religion Act, 2021, does not apply in this case because there is no evidence that the conversions were carried out by force, fraud, coercion, or deception.

“Prima facie, from the averments made in the writ petition, it appears that both the corpus are major women who are legally competent to take independent decisions concerning their faith, marriage, residence, and future course of life. The pleadings further disclose that they have voluntarily renounced the Hindu religion, embraced Islam, and expressed their desire to solemnise marriage according to their own wishes,” court said.

It added that if the If the assertions made by the petitioners are ultimately found to be correct, then interference with such personal choices could amount to an infringement of their constitutionally protected rights to dignity, privacy, personal liberty and decisional autonomy.

“Their production before this Court, therefore, becomes imperative to enable the Court to interact with them directly and to satisfy itself regarding the voluntariness of their decisions and the legality of their present custody,” court said while directing for their production on next date of hearing, on August 6.

The court further ordered that if the women are not produced on the scheduled date, the concerned police officials must file personal affidavits explaining the reasons for non-compliance and detailing the steps taken to secure their production.

World.title: Govt cuts petrol price by 12 paisas, diesel by 66 paisas for the next three days
World.content:
The government on Friday reduced the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by 12 paisas and 66 paisas per litre, respectively.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs336.03 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs392.38 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs110 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs96 per litre on diesel.

The Petroleum Division’s notification said that the new prices would be applicable from August 1 to August 3.

Meanwhile, in a bigger price shock, the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) notified a record 32pc increase in the price of regasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) for August, taking it to $25.83 per mmBtu for SNGPL and $25.09 per mmBtu for SSGCL.

This will translate into a retail price of Rs7,204 per mmBtu. The price is based on five imported cargoes from the spot market, as no shipment could be secured from Qatar because of the US-Iran war. This is the single biggest jump in RLNG rates in its decade-long history.

This comes on top of an about 15pc increase in the RLNG price fixed last month at $19.52 per mmBtu (Rs5,446 per mmBtu) for SNGPL and $18.63 per mmBtu for SSGCL.

Compared with $10.45 (Rs2,916) per mmBtu in February this year, the RLNG price hike works out to around 148pc for August.

This mainly results in a substantial increase in fuel costs for power generation. This can be seen from the fact that the fuel cost for RLNG-based power generation in May worked out to Rs31 per unit, compared with Rs13.72 per unit in April.

The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan this week.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Search operation for climbers missing after Broad Peak avalanche suspended due to bad weather
World.content:
GILGIT: The search and rescue operation for foreign climbers missing after an avalanche at Broad Peak was suspended late Friday due to adverse weather conditions in the region.

Three bodies of missing climbers — one each from the United States, Nepal and Oman — were airlifted from Broad Peak to Skardu by Pakistan Army helicopters. Drone footage also indicated the presence of more climbers during the search operation.

Earlier reports had said that four bodies were recovered; however, the toll was later revised down to three. Seven climbers remain missing.

According to a press release issued by the Commissioner Baltistan Division, the search and rescue operation was launched following a formal request from tour operators.

A three-member civil rescue team, led by renowned mountaineer Sarbaz Khan, was airlifted to Broad Peak Base Camp by Pakistan Army Aviation helicopters.

The team recovered the bodies of three climbers, identified as Oman’s Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy, Nepal’s Pur Bahadur Gurung and Mallory Geis from the United States. The bodies were later shifted to CMH Skardu by Pakistan Army Aviation helicopters.

The press release said the rescue operation had been temporarily suspended due to poor weather conditions and would resume on Saturday once conditions improved. Other Sherpas involved in mountaineering expeditions at the peak would also assist in the operation.

The rescue team said signs indicating the presence of more climbers had also been spotted through drone footage.

Despite the challenging terrain and harsh weather conditions at such high altitudes, the search operation was continuing with the cooperation of the Pakistan Army, local expert mountaineers and rescue teams.

The Gilgit-Baltistan government expressed condolences to the families of the deceased climbers and assured them that all possible assistance would be provided in the rescue operation and the repatriation of the bodies to their respective countries.
